versions.title: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government Version 2.0
versions.summary: December 2025 update strengthening AI governance: strategic approach to adoption, operationalised responsible AI, designated use-case accountability and risk-based use-case-level actions.

changes.detail: Agencies must develop a strategic position on AI adoption within 6 months
Approach to operationalise responsible AI (incl. staff/public reporting pathways and AI incident processes)
Accountable use case owners and an internal register of in-scope AI use cases shared with the DTA every 6 months
In-scope criteria and mandatory AI use case impact assessment, with extra governance for high-risk use cases

versions.note: Changes summarised from the policy introduction; the document does not give a detailed change log versus v1.1.

covered_entities: accountable officials and accountable use case owners
covered_systems: AI systems as defined by the OECD
in-scope AI use cases (Appendix C criteria)
general-purpose AI solutions such as Microsoft Copilot (single complex use case or separate use cases)
covered_activities: AI use case registration and impact assessment
deployment, monitoring and review of AI use cases
exceptions: use of AI in the defence portfolio
national intelligence community (Office of National Intelligence Act 2018 s4)
early-stage experimentation meeting Appendix C conditions
incidental lower-risk AI use (e.g. grammar checks, AI-enabled search)
conditions: use-case-level actions apply to in-scope AI use cases meeting any Appendix C criterion
additional governance, DTA reporting and 12-monthly review for inherent high-risk use cases
implementation deadlines of 6 or 12 months from 15 December 2025; existing use cases by 30 April 2027
documents.objective: Provide a coordinated framework for accelerated, sustainable AI adoption by Australian Government agencies while ensuring safe, ethical and responsible use through transparency, accountability and risk-based oversight of AI use cases.

related_policies.policy: Policy for the responsible use of AI in government v1.1 (DTA, 2024)

documents.conflict_rule: Designed to complement and strengthen, not duplicate, existing frameworks and laws; must be read and applied alongside them (e.g. Privacy Act 1988, Protective Security Policy Framework, APS Code of Conduct).

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/aus-gov.pdf). PDF footer reads '© Commonwealth of Australia (Digital Transformation Agency) 2025 | Version 1801'; PDF metadata creation date 28 Nov 2025. No official URL is printed in the document, so source_uri points to the asago copy. Binding=false: not legislation, but mandatory for non-corporate Commonwealth entities as whole-of-government policy. Not verified whether v2.0 is still the latest version. Year in policy_id is the v2.0 issue/effective year (2025). The OECD AI definition is adopted (hence the link to OECD_AI_Principles_2019); Australia's AI Ethics Principles are referenced as material staff must be informed about.

clauses.section: Strategy and oversight – Mandatory requirements – AI transparency statement
clauses.original_text: Agencies must make a publicly available statement outlining their approach to AI adoption and use, as prescribed under the Standard for transparency statements. The statement must be reviewed and updated annually or sooner, should the agency make significant changes to its approach to AI.
clauses.requirement: publish a public AI transparency statement per the Standard for transparency statements and review it at least annually
clauses.purpose: build public trust through transparency about government AI use
clauses.applicable_systems: AI use cases of non-corporate Commonwealth entities
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the Version 2.0 PDF (pdftotext extraction); line breaks collapsed. The following sentence also requires agencies to notify the DTA of publication and changes.

clauses.section: Strategy and oversight – Mandatory requirements – Accountable officials / Accountable use case owners
clauses.original_text: Agencies must designate accountable official(s) to take accountability for implementing this policy. … Agencies must designate an accountable use case owner for each in-scope AI use case within 12 months of this policy taking effect.
clauses.object: accountable official(s) and accountable use case owners
clauses.requirement: designate accountable official(s) for the policy and an accountable owner for each in-scope AI use case, following the Standard for accountability
clauses.condition: use case owners: in-scope AI use cases; within 12 months of 15 December 2025
clauses.applicable_systems: AI use cases of non-corporate Commonwealth entities
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the Version 2.0 PDF (pdftotext extraction); line breaks collapsed. Responsibilities are set in the separate Standard for accountability, not reproduced in this document.

clauses.section: Preparedness and operations – Mandatory requirements – Operationalise the responsible use of AI
clauses.original_text: Agencies must establish an approach to embed responsible AI practices within 12 months of this policy taking effect. … At a minimum, the approach will provide an agency with: … a pathway for staff to report AI safety concerns, including AI incidents. pathways for the public to report AI safety concerns, appropriate to the agency’s AI use. clear processes to address AI incidents aligned to their ICT incident management approach - incident remediation must be overseen by an appropriate governance body or senior executive and should be undertaken in line with any other legal obligations.
clauses.object: approach to embed responsible AI practices, including AI incident reporting and handling
clauses.requirement: within 12 months, establish staff and public pathways to report AI safety concerns and incidents, and incident processes with senior oversight of remediation
clauses.condition: within 12 months of the policy taking effect
clauses.purpose: protect Australians from AI harms; manage AI incidents
clauses.affected_asset: persons affected by government AI; agency operations
clauses.applicable_systems: AI use cases of non-corporate Commonwealth entities
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the Version 2.0 PDF (pdftotext extraction); line breaks collapsed. Bullet list flattened; other bullets (adoption process, informing staff about Australia's AI Ethics Principles) elided. 'AI incident' is defined in Appendix B (adapted from the OECD draft definition).

clauses.section: Preparedness and operations – Mandatory requirements – Staff training on AI
clauses.original_text: Agencies must implement mandatory training for all staff on responsible AI use within 12 months of this policy taking effect.
clauses.requirement: mandatory responsible-AI training for all staff within 12 months (the AI fundamentals module may be used)
clauses.condition: within 12 months of the policy taking effect
clauses.purpose: AI capability and responsible use by APS officers
clauses.applicable_systems: all agency AI use
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the Version 2.0 PDF (pdftotext extraction); line breaks collapsed. Additional role-based training (procurement, development, deployment) is a SHOULD.

clauses.section: AI use case impact assessment – Mandatory requirements – All new AI use cases / In-scope AI use cases
clauses.original_text: For AI use cases that are in-scope, agencies must conduct an AI use case impact assessment. Agencies are to commence an assessment at the design stage. Before the solution is deployed, agencies must finalise the assessment and apply any agreed risk treatments.
clauses.action: conduct impact assessment and apply risk treatments
clauses.requirement: assess all new AI use cases against the in-scope criteria; for in-scope ones complete an impact assessment (DTA tool or equivalent) and apply agreed treatments before deployment
clauses.condition: use case meets any Appendix C criterion (e.g. more than insignificant harm, materially influences administrative decisions, public interaction without human review, personal/sensitive or classified data)
clauses.exception: early-stage experimentation that does not commit to the use case, risk harm or introduce privacy/security risks (Appendix C)
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, communities, First Nations collective rights
clauses.applicable_systems: AI use cases of non-corporate Commonwealth entities
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the Version 2.0 PDF (pdftotext extraction); line breaks collapsed. Existing unassessed use cases must be brought into compliance by 30 April 2027.

clauses.section: AI use case impact assessment – Mandatory requirements – High-risk AI use cases
clauses.original_text: If an agency determines their in-scope AI use case has an inherent high-risk rating when completing an AI use case impact assessment, they must: report the use case to the agency accountable official with the reasons for the inherent high-risk rating, proposed mitigations and residual risks govern the use case through a designated board or a senior executive, whichever is appropriate for the size and scope of the agency. Once an agency has decided to deploy the use case, they must: report the use case to the DTA through the accountable official, see the Standard for accountability establish a system to regularly review the use case every 12 months at a minimum.
clauses.recipient: accountable official; DTA; governing board / senior executive
clauses.requirement: escalate high-risk use cases, place them under board/senior-executive governance, report deployment to the DTA and review at least every 12 months
clauses.condition: inherent high-risk rating in the AI use case impact assessment
clauses.purpose: additional oversight of higher-risk AI; ensure use case operates as intended and risks are managed
clauses.affected_asset: individuals and communities affected by high-risk government AI
clauses.applicable_systems: high-risk in-scope AI use cases
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the Version 2.0 PDF (pdftotext extraction); line breaks collapsed. Bullets flattened without separators. The review must report whether the use case operates as intended and risks are effectively managed.

locale_context.regulation: Self-regulation · mandatory group-wide corporate policy built on the EU AI Act
locale_context.culture: European travel-tech multinational that extends EU AI Act categories (prohibited, high-risk, transparency) group-wide as a compliance-first internal rulebook, combined with a GenAI acceptable-use policy and a central use-case review board.

key_dates.event: Policy dated 10 December 2024 (cover page)

versions.title: Amadeus AI Policy, 10 December 2024
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_entities: employees and contractors of Amadeus IT Group SA and its affiliated companies
insofar as possible, non-fully owned companies and distributors
covered_systems: AI tools (AI systems and AI models), incl. ML, logic-based, LLM and generative AI, recommender, chatbots, agents, recognition and analytics systems
GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology on company or personal devices used for work
covered_activities: procurement, deployment and use of AI tools
conditions: Annex 1 high-risk use cases require prior Legal approval; prohibited practices barred in all cases
use of unapproved GenAI tools tolerated only with [PUBLIC] data
documents.objective: Set a group-wide framework for ethical and lawful development, deployment and use of AI at Amadeus, aligned with the EU AI Act, including a Generative AI Acceptable Use Policy and a list of prohibited and high-risk use cases.

related_policies.policy: EU AI Pact (voluntary pledges; Amadeus is a signatory)

documents.conflict_rule: Applies in addition to other Amadeus policies on the same subjects (AI security standard, security and privacy policies); approval by the AI Use Case Review Board does not exempt other processes.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/amadeus.pdf). The document carries only the date 10 December 2024 and no version number or change history; effective date assumed to be that date. Not checked whether a newer version exists. binding=false (not law), but the policy is mandatory for employees and contractors: non-compliance can lead to disciplinary action up to termination, and contractor violations may be treated as breach of contract. Referenced annexes/intranet documents (GenAI Acceptable Use Framework, AI Security Standard) are not included in the copy.

clauses.original_text: Do not input sensitive information or personal data into non-approved Gen AI Tools.
clauses.requirement: never put non-public information or personal data into non-approved GenAI tools
clauses.condition: when using non-approved GenAI Tools
clauses.purpose: avoid exposing company, customer and employee data to third parties via model training/outputs
clauses.affected_asset: confidential information; personal data of customers and employees
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI Tools (GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology), approved or publicly available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Sensitive information = anything not classified [PUBLIC] under the Information Classification and Asset Management Policy, incl. personal data and third-party proprietary information. Use of unapproved tools is tolerated only with [PUBLIC] data.

clauses.original_text: The following practices are strictly prohibited (under the EU AI Act and can result in fines of up to 7% of the total worldwide annual turnover of Amadeus. No one within Amadeus may therefore engage in these practices under any circumstances, including through AI Tools which have been approved: a. Subliminal, manipulative and/or deceptive techniques with the risk of significant harm. … c. Biometric categorization to infer sensitive personal traits. … d. Classification or scoring of people based on behavior or personality characteristics leading to detrimental treatment. … h. Inferring emotions in workplaces and education.
clauses.object: EU AI Act prohibited AI practices (items a–h)
clauses.requirement: no development or deployment of manipulative, exploitative, biometric-categorisation, social-scoring, real-time RBI, predictive-policing, face-scraping or workplace emotion-recognition AI
clauses.purpose: comply with EU AI Act Art. 5 and protect fundamental rights
clauses.affected_asset: natural persons' fundamental rights and autonomy
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI tool, including approved ones
clauses.interpretation_notes: Annex 1 restates the EU AI Act Article 5 prohibitions with travel/industry examples; applied Group-wide, not only in the EU. Items b, e, f and g and the per-item examples elided. The source has an unclosed parenthesis after 'prohibited', kept as printed.

clauses.section: III. General rules for deployment/use of all AI tools
clauses.original_text: All uses of AI tools procured/ deployed by Amadeus need to be registered in the Amadeus AI Inventory. Employees shall log their use case for review and approval of the AI Use Case Review Board: LOP - AI Use Case Intake - Power Apps. This step is mandatory.
clauses.requirement: register every AI use case in the AI Inventory and obtain AI Use Case Review Board approval
clauses.condition: before procuring/deploying an AI tool
clauses.purpose: risk-categorise use cases and route them to the right review
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (AI systems and models) developed, procured or deployed by the Amadeus Group
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mandatory gate; separately, use cases on the Annex 1 high-risk list need prior Legal approval and prohibited ones may not be procured at all. Board approval does not exempt other processes (IT, CISO, Privacy).

clauses.section: III. General rules for deployment/use of all AI tools
clauses.original_text: We should therefore assign human oversight for the deployment of AI tools to persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support to carry out this oversight well. Generally, everyone who operates the tool should be able to understand how it should work in order to be able to notice when outputs are unreliable and avoid over-reliance on the outputs.
clauses.requirement: competent, trained and authorised humans oversee AI deployments; operators understand the tool to avoid over-reliance
clauses.purpose: catch blind spots, biases and unreliable outputs
clauses.affected_asset: persons affected by AI outputs; Amadeus
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools (AI systems and models) developed, procured or deployed by the Amadeus Group
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mirrors EU AI Act deployer duties (Art. 26). Framed as 'should' within a mandatory policy.

clauses.original_text: Do clearly attribute any output used for business purposes to the GenAI application that created it through a footnote or other means visible to the reader. … all GenAI generated content must be disclosed, cited and reviewed if used for business purposes (e.g. any purpose related to your work at Amadeus) to enable end-users to determine how to consume the content in an informed manner.
clauses.object: GenAI-generated content used for business purposes
clauses.requirement: visibly attribute GenAI output to the tool that produced it and review it before business use
clauses.condition: if used for business purposes
clauses.purpose: transparency to readers and protection against IP claims
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI Tools (GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology), approved or publicly available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Same section also requires keeping an updated record of GenAI use for business purposes.

clauses.section: IV.2.3 Be critical of outputs and carefully use them
clauses.original_text: Do not use any output that contains material that you suspect to be under copyright protection in any materials, internal or externally facing. … Do not use GenAI Tools to create text, audio, or visual content for purposes of committing fraud or to misrepresent an individual’s identity.
clauses.object: GenAI output suspected to be copyrighted; content for fraud or identity misrepresentation
clauses.requirement: no use of suspected-copyright output; no GenAI content for fraud or impersonation
clauses.purpose: avoid IP infringement and fraudulent or deceptive use
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI Tools (GenAI Solutions and GenAI Technology), approved or publicly available
clauses.interpretation_notes: Two bullets from the same list; the elided bullet forbids relying on information suspected to be inaccurate, inappropriate or biased.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/ars.md). The copy combines an introductory post by Ken Fisher with the policy itself; clauses are taken from the policy part only. The policy states it was last updated April 22, 2026; no first-publication or effective date is given (the intro says the standards have governed editorial work since AI tooling became available, and the reader-facing version is a translation of an internal policy), so effective_date is null. The document says changes will be noted on the policy page; not checked whether a later update exists. binding=false; the standards are mandatory for Ars editorial staff and contributors ('When violations occur, we take action').

clauses.original_text: Ars Technica’s editorial text is written by humans. We do not use AI to generate our reporting, analysis, or commentary.
clauses.actor: Ars Technica writers, editors and contributors
clauses.requirement: editorial text is human-written; AI is not used to generate journalism
clauses.exception: AI output reproduced as exemplar material when AI is the subject of reporting
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used in Ars Technica's editorial workflow
clauses.interpretation_notes: Exception: AI output may be reproduced when it is itself the subject of reporting, set apart and disclosed; AI editing aids (grammar, style, structure) may recommend but not make changes.

clauses.original_text: AI tools must not be used to generate, extract, or summarize material that is then attributed to a named source, whether as a direct quote, a paraphrase, or a characterization of someone’s views.
clauses.object: material attributed to a named source
clauses.requirement: attributed quotes, paraphrases and characterisations must come from direct engagement with the source material
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used in Ars Technica's editorial workflow
clauses.interpretation_notes: Attributed material must come from interviews, transcripts, published statements or documents reviewed by the reporter.

clauses.original_text: Even then, AI output is never treated as an authoritative source. Everything must be verified. … We don’t publish claims based solely on AI-generated summaries, and reporters may not represent any material as “reviewed” unless they have examined it directly.
clauses.requirement: verify all AI research output; no claims based solely on AI summaries
clauses.condition: when AI tools are used to assist research
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools vetted and approved for the Ars workflow (research, summarising, dataset search)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Research use is limited to tools vetted and approved for the workflow.

clauses.original_text: Every author who uses AI tools in the course of reporting a story must disclose that use to their editors, and authors remain fully responsible for their content.
clauses.object: use of AI tools in reporting
clauses.requirement: internal disclosure of AI use to editors; author retains full responsibility
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used in Ars Technica's editorial workflow
clauses.interpretation_notes: Internal (to editors), not reader-facing, disclosure. Section 'Accountability is non-negotiable' adds that responsibility cannot be transferred to colleagues, editors or tools.

clauses.original_text: We do not publish AI-generated images, audio, or video as authentic documentation of real events. We do not alter documentary media in ways that change their meaning.
clauses.actor: Ars Technica editorial and art teams
clauses.requirement: no synthetic media presented as real; no meaning-changing edits to documentary media
clauses.exception: standard production work such as color correction, cropping and contrast adjustments
clauses.purpose: prevent misleading the public about real events
clauses.applicable_systems: image, audio and video generation tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Standard production work (colour correction, cropping, contrast) is expressly allowed.

clauses.original_text: When synthetic media is used in the context of reporting on AI, it will be clearly identified as AI-generated, with that disclosure placed as close to the material as possible.
clauses.object: synthetic media used in reporting on AI
clauses.requirement: clear AI-generated label placed next to the material
clauses.condition: when synthetic media is used in reporting on AI
clauses.applicable_systems: AI-generated images, audio and video
clauses.interpretation_notes: Framed as 'will be' (a commitment); treated as mandatory.

clauses.original_text: If Supplier seeks permission according to the above section 1.1., Supplier shall provide Cisco with all information and assistance reasonably required by Cisco to (i) comply with Applicable Laws, and (ii) perform all types of assessments and related diligence that Cisco deems necessary.

clauses.requirement: support Cisco's legal compliance and diligence before permission is granted
clauses.condition: if Supplier seeks permission under 1.1
clauses.purpose: lawful, assessed use of Protected Data for AI training

clauses.interpretation_notes: Process requirement attached to the permission route in 1.1.

clauses.original_text: A permission granted by Cisco according to section 1.1. is limited to one (1) year, unless otherwise agreed upon between the Parties.

clauses.exception: otherwise agreed between the Parties

clauses.original_text: If Supplier is using or intends to use Artificial Intelligence and/or Machine Learning technologies in the course of Performing, it is required to have an AI/ML governance program in place, with defined policies and procedures, that meets or exceeds current best industry standards.

clauses.requirement: AI/ML governance program meeting or exceeding current best industry standards

The copy has only 3 pages (it ends after Rule 4 on p. 3) and is partly redacted (footnotes 3, 5 and 7 and some links blacked out), so later rules, if any, are missing. Page 2 has no text layer; its text was transcribed from the page image. The document cites the AI Act as 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1624' (the AI Act is Regulation (EU) 2024/1689); recorded as EU_AI_Act_2024. Titled 'guidelines', but the content is mandatory staff rules ('Rule n°1–4', 'staff must'), so recorded as an internal policy; binding=false because it is not law. Whether a later version exists was not checked.

clauses.section: 2.1 [Rule n°1] Use Commission internal AI tools as the first choice.
clauses.original_text: For any work-related task involving generative AI, staff must use the Commission’s internal tools as the default option and follow their terms and conditions. These tools operate in controlled IT environments. External AI tools may only be considered if no suitable internal alternative is available.
clauses.object: generative AI tools for work tasks
clauses.requirement: internal tools as default; external tools only if no suitable internal alternative
clauses.condition: any work-related task involving generative AI
clauses.exception: no suitable internal alternative available
clauses.purpose: keep Commission information in controlled IT environments
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 2 (the copy has no text layer on that page); bold emphasis omitted.

clauses.section: 2.2 [Rule n°2] Do not use non-public or personal data in external AI tools and ensure proper handling of sensitive and personal data when using internal AI tools.
clauses.original_text: Never input into external AI tools any information that is not already public or any personal data (4). … However, the handling of Classified information is strictly prohibited in any generative AI tool, including Commission-internal ones.
clauses.object: non-public information or personal data (external tools); classified information (any tool)
clauses.requirement: no non-public or personal data in external tools; no classified information in any GenAI tool
clauses.exception: pre-authorised scientific projects involving evaluation, testing or benchmarking of AI (footnote 4)
clauses.purpose: prevent disclosure and reuse of internal information by service providers
clauses.affected_asset: non-public Commission information; personal data; classified information
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 2 (the copy has no text layer on that page); bold emphasis omitted. Footnote marker '(4)' kept.

clauses.original_text: In addition, a human review of outputs is necessary to comply with the principle of accuracy and transparency regarding the use of generative AI tools. Further, it is not permitted to subject individuals to decisions which produce legal effects based solely on automated processing.
clauses.action: review outputs; do not make solely automated decisions
clauses.object: generative AI outputs; decisions producing legal effects
clauses.requirement: human review of outputs; no solely automated decisions with legal effects
clauses.condition: where personal data is processed
clauses.purpose: data-protection accuracy and rights of individuals
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 2 (the copy has no text layer on that page); bold emphasis omitted. Set in the context of personal data processing under data protection rules (Regulation 2018/1725).

clauses.section: 2.3 [Rule n°3] Always critically assess AI outputs for accuracy and bias.
clauses.original_text: Do not rely on AI tools as authoritative sources. Staff must always verify all AI-generated content, even when it appears coherent and confident, before using it further in Commission work. … Staff remain fully responsible for the final result.
clauses.object: AI-generated content incl. sources and references
clauses.requirement: verify all AI output and treat it as an initial draft; staff remain responsible
clauses.condition: before further use in Commission work
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Applies to internal and external tools alike.

clauses.section: 2.4 [Rule n°4] Be mindful of potential intellectual property rights violations and avoid directly replicating the output of a generative AI tool in public documents.
clauses.original_text: Always assess whether generated output might violate intellectual property rights. … Moreover, outputs from generative AI tools should not be copy-pasted in documents meant to be published. Exceptions can be considered if such output is based solely on documents owned by or duly licensed to the Commission (e.g. an official text translated via eTranslation).
clauses.action: assess IP; do not copy-paste into published documents
clauses.requirement: assess outputs for IP infringement; no direct replication in public documents
clauses.condition: documents meant to be published
clauses.exception: output based solely on Commission-owned or duly licensed documents
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Particular caution for drafting legislative texts; contact the Central IP Service when in doubt.

The prohibited-practices list in s.5.1 closely mirrors EU AI Act Article 5, though the policy only cites the Act among its sources. Binding=false: not law; the policy is addressed to all ICRC staff.

clauses.section: 5.1 A humanitarian and principled approach – Humanity
clauses.original_text: In light of the above, the ICRC will refrain from using, deploying or providing AI systems that: deploy subliminal, manipulative, or deceptive techniques to distort behaviour and impair informed decision-making; exploit vulnerabilities related to age, disability, or socio-economic circumstances to distort behaviour; use biometric categorization systems that infer sensitive personal attributes, except for labelling or filtering lawfully acquired biometric datasets; rely on or infer social scoring, (i.e. evaluating or classifying individuals or groups based on social behaviour or personal traits); assess the risk of an individual committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits, except when used to augment human assessments; compile facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage; or infer emotions, except for medical or safety reasons.
clauses.action: refrain from using, deploying or providing
clauses.object: manipulative, exploitative, biometric-categorisation, social-scoring, predictive-policing, facial-scraping and emotion-recognition AI systems
clauses.requirement: do not use, deploy or provide listed prohibited categories of AI
clauses.exception: labelling/filtering lawfully acquired biometric datasets; risk assessment that augments human assessment; emotion inference for medical or safety reasons
clauses.purpose: protect dignity, agency and rights of affected people
clauses.affected_asset: affected people's autonomy, privacy and rights
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems used, deployed or provided by the ICRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. List closely mirrors EU AI Act Art. 5 prohibitions, with similar carve-outs.

clauses.section: 5.1 A humanitarian and principled approach – Impartiality
clauses.original_text: The ICRC acknowledges the significant risks of AI systems that could generate false or inaccurate data and replicate or amplify systemic and societal discriminations, biases and stereotypes – in particular around gender and race. We make proactive and sustained efforts to understand, avoid and mitigate these risks through our choice and use of AI solutions, and by avoiding their use where these biases cannot be effectively avoided or mitigated.
clauses.action: understand, avoid and mitigate; avoid use
clauses.object: bias, discrimination and inaccuracy in AI systems
clauses.requirement: mitigate bias and inaccuracy; do not use AI where bias cannot be effectively mitigated
clauses.affected_asset: affected populations (especially regarding gender and race)
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions chosen and used by the ICRC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. Framed as a commitment ('we make … efforts'); the refusal to use AI where bias cannot be mitigated is close to a MUST NOT.

clauses.original_text: At all times, the ICRC ensures that confidential or sensitive internal ICRC information or personal data are handled with the utmost care and are not used in or transferred to non-approved, external online AI systems, in line with the duty of discretion stated in the ICRC’s Code of Conduct.
clauses.object: confidential or sensitive internal information or personal data
clauses.requirement: no confidential/sensitive information or personal data in non-approved external online AI systems
clauses.affected_asset: confidential ICRC information; personal data of affected people
clauses.applicable_systems: non-approved, external online AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. s.6.4 adds that staff must not input critical humanitarian, (strictly) confidential or IP-protected information into external or commercial online AI services.

clauses.original_text: Additional systematic data quality control and meaningful and effective human oversight mechanisms are put in place to control and review relevant training models, algorithmic systems, inputs and outputs throughout the lifecycle of AI solutions used to support operational activities and decision-making processes that have an impact and present a risk of harm for affected people and users.
clauses.action: put in place human oversight and data quality control
clauses.object: training models, algorithmic systems, inputs and outputs
clauses.requirement: meaningful human oversight and data quality control throughout the lifecycle of impactful AI
clauses.condition: where AI supports operational activities or decisions that have an impact and present a risk of harm
clauses.applicable_systems: AI supporting operational activities and decision-making with risk of harm
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. Descriptive present tense in an aspirational policy; read as SHOULD.

clauses.original_text: Relevant and intelligible information about the use of AI systems is systematically provided to affected people and users when these systems could have an impact on them or their rights, or when decisions with significant consequences for the organization are concerned.
clauses.requirement: inform affected people and users about AI use where it may affect them or their rights
clauses.condition: when systems could impact them or their rights, or for decisions with significant consequences for the organization
clauses.purpose: transparency and accountability to affected people
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems that could impact affected people or their rights
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from a plain pdftotext re-extraction of the asago PDF (two-column layout); line breaks and hyphenation joined, bullet markers dropped. The next bullet extends this to why, when and how AI is used and explanations of the input-output link.

clauses.original_text: All possible efforts are made to integrate and mitigate the environmental impact and carbon footprint of considered AI solutions through a life-cycle approach. This includes favouring solutions and tools that have a lighter footprint, in line with the ICRC’s Plan of Action under the Climate and Environment Charter for Humanitarian Organizations and the ICRC’s Framework for Sustainable Development.
clauses.action: mitigate environmental impact; favour lighter-footprint tools
clauses.requirement: life-cycle mitigation of AI environmental impact and carbon footprint

covered_entities: organizations that develop, produce, deploy or use products, systems and services that utilize AI
covered_systems: AI systems and AI-enabled products and services

risk identification, analysis, evaluation and treatment
conditions: Guidance only ('should' statements); intended to be tailored to the organization and its context
documents.objective: Provide guidance on how organizations can manage risks specifically related to AI and integrate risk management into AI-related activities and functions, by adapting the principles, framework and process of ISO 31000:2018 to AI.
documents.conflict_rule: Guidance standard; does not override legal requirements. Should be read with ISO 31000:2018, whose structure it follows.

sources_consulted: https://www.iso.org/standard/77304.html (catalogue page, via search results only)
record_provenance.notes: Paywalled standard: official text not accessed; all clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false). Structure (Clause 4 Principles, Clause 5 Framework, Clause 6 Risk management process; Annex B risk sources; Annex C risk management and AI system life cycle) corroborated by the ANSI preview and OECD.AI summaries per search results. Annex A topic (AI-related objectives) reported inconsistently by secondary sources. Exact publication day not verified (only YYYY-MM given). Secondary sources (2026) report no amendment or revision in progress; a CEN adoption as EN ISO/IEC 23894 was mentioned by one source but could not be verified. Principles list mirrors ISO 31000:2018 principles, which 23894 adopts with AI-specific commentary. Official languages: only English edition confirmed.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] Top management should demonstrate leadership and commitment by integrating AI risk management into all organizational activities, issuing a statement or policy establishing an AI risk management approach, allocating resources, and assigning authority, responsibility and accountability for managing AI risks at appropriate levels.
clauses.action: demonstrate leadership, allocate resources, assign accountability
clauses.requirement: integrate AI risk management with clear accountability and resources
clauses.purpose: embed AI risk management in governance
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems in organizational scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase following ISO 31000 clause 5.2 with AI-specific additions; subclause heading believed correct but not verified against the official text.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should define the scope of its AI risk management activities, understand the external and internal context (including applicable legal requirements, stakeholder expectations and the AI system's intended purpose and use), and define risk criteria, including the amount and type of risk it may or may not take, taking into account impacts on individuals, groups and society.
clauses.action: define scope, context and risk criteria
clauses.requirement: set scope, context and risk criteria before assessing AI risk
clauses.purpose: tailor risk management to AI context
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, groups, society and the organization
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems in organizational scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; mirrors ISO 31000 6.3.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should identify AI-related risks by considering assets and their value, risk sources (e.g. complexity of the environment, lack of transparency and explainability, level of automation, machine learning-specific issues, system hardware, lifecycle issues and technology readiness), potential events and outcomes, controls in place, and consequences for the organization, individuals and society.
clauses.object: AI risk sources, events, outcomes and consequences
clauses.requirement: systematically identify AI risks using AI-specific risk sources
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems in organizational scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; the listed risk sources correspond to Annex B as summarized in secondary sources and should be verified.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should select and implement options for treating AI risks (e.g. avoiding the risk, removing the risk source, changing likelihood or consequences, sharing the risk, or retaining it by informed decision), prepare risk treatment plans, and assess whether residual risk is acceptable, taking into account AI-specific considerations.
clauses.requirement: treat AI risks and evaluate residual risk
clauses.condition: where risks exceed risk criteria
clauses.purpose: reduce AI risks to acceptable levels
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems in organizational scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; treatment options follow ISO 31000 6.5.2.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization should monitor and review the AI risk management process and its outcomes on an ongoing and periodic basis throughout the AI system life cycle, recognizing that AI systems and their context can change over time (e.g. through continuous learning or data drift).
clauses.object: AI risk management process and outcomes
clauses.requirement: continuously and periodically monitor AI risks across the lifecycle
clauses.purpose: keep risk management effective as AI systems evolve
clauses.affected_asset: AI system reliability and affected stakeholders
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems in organizational scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; Annex C maps risk management activities to AI lifecycle stages.

documents.objective: Specify requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system within an organization, so that AI systems are developed, provided or used responsibly in pursuit of the organization's objectives and in line with stakeholder expectations.

sources_consulted: https://www.iso.org/standard/81230.html (catalogue page, via search results only)
Secondary summaries surfaced via web search (e.g. docs.modulos.ai ISO 42001 pages, gaicc.org status page)
record_provenance.notes: Paywalled standard: the official text was not accessed; all clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false) based on the standard's well-known clause structure as corroborated by secondary sources. iso.org could not be fetched from this session. Secondary sources (Sept–Oct 2026) report no amendment or revision registered. Exact publication day (believed 18 Dec 2023) not verified, so only YYYY-MM is given. Normative status of Annexes is reported inconsistently in secondary sources; this record treats Annex A (reference control objectives and controls) as normative, which should be checked. Secondary sources count 38 Annex A controls under 9 objectives (A.2–A.10). Official languages: ISO publishes in English and French; French edition availability not verified.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] Top management shall establish an AI policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization, provides a framework for setting AI objectives, includes a commitment to meet applicable requirements and a commitment to continual improvement of the AI management system; the policy shall be documented, communicated within the organization and available to interested parties as appropriate.
clauses.requirement: establish a documented AI policy with commitments to applicable requirements and continual improvement
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.purpose: set direction and accountability for responsible AI
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase of harmonized-structure clause; 'shall' requirements are binding only for conformity/certification, hence MUST within the standard's own logic although the standard is voluntary.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define and establish an AI risk assessment process that is informed by its AI policy and objectives, produces consistent, valid and comparable results, identifies risks that could aid or prevent achieving AI objectives, analyses potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies together with their likelihood, and evaluates and prioritizes risks against risk criteria; documented information on the process shall be retained.
clauses.requirement: run a documented, repeatable AI risk assessment covering consequences for the organization, individuals and society
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.affected_asset: individuals, groups, societies and the organization
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; the standard refers to ISO/IEC 23894 for further guidance on AI risk management.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define an AI risk treatment process to select treatment options, determine the necessary controls, compare them with the controls in Annex A to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted, and produce a Statement of Applicability containing the necessary controls and justification for inclusion or exclusion; it shall formulate a risk treatment plan and obtain approval of residual risks from designated management.
clauses.action: select treatments, determine controls, produce Statement of Applicability
clauses.requirement: treat AI risks with controls cross-checked against Annex A and document a Statement of Applicability
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.exception: Annex A controls may be excluded with documented justification
clauses.purpose: ensure appropriate controls for identified AI risks
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; mirrors ISO/IEC 27001 6.1.3 mechanics.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall define a process for assessing the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, and for societies, that can result from the development, provision or use of AI systems, taking into account the technical and societal context and applicable jurisdictions; the results shall be documented and considered in the risk assessment.
clauses.object: impacts of AI systems on individuals, groups and societies
clauses.requirement: perform and document AI system impact assessments feeding into risk assessment
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.purpose: protect individuals and society from adverse AI impacts
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; operationalized in Clause 8.4 and Annex A.5; detailed guidance in ISO/IEC 42005:2025.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the AI management system conforms to the organization's own requirements and to the requirements of the standard, and is effectively implemented and maintained.
clauses.requirement: audit the AIMS at planned intervals
clauses.condition: for organizations claiming conformity
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems within the AIMS scope
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase of harmonized-structure clause common to ISO management system standards.

LLVM copyright and license policy (Developer Policy)

documents.conflict_rule: Copyright treatment follows the project's general copyright policy; enforcement is left to maintainers' judgment.

sources_consulted: http://llvm.org/docs/AIToolPolicy.html (URL printed in the policy; not fetched)
record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/llvm.md). (asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper commit b8ac8876beec6593ef5685d7d7e64cc94f9cc55b.) The document states no adoption date or version; the only date is a reference 'fetched 2025-10-01', so the version date 2025-10 is an inference (policy adopted no earlier than October 2025) and effective_date is left null. The printed official URL (llvm.org/docs/AIToolPolicy.html) is used as source_uri but was not fetched, so whether the online text has since changed is unverified. Binding=false: not law; mandatory for contributors and enforced by maintainers (request changes, 'extractive' label, escalation to moderators, removal of infringing contributions). Some text is acknowledged as copied from the Fedora policy proposal (CC BY 4.0).

clauses.original_text: Contributors must read and review all LLM-generated code or text before they ask other project members to review it. The contributor is always the author and is fully accountable for their contributions.
clauses.requirement: self-review of all LLM output before requesting review; contributor is author and accountable
clauses.purpose: quality and accountability; protect maintainer time
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs, coding assistants, AI agents and automated review tools used for LLVM contributions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Contributors should also be able to answer questions about their work during review.

clauses.original_text: Contributors are expected to be transparent and label contributions that contain substantial amounts of tool-generated content. … Contributors should note tool usage in their pull request description, commit message, or wherever authorship is normally indicated for the work.
clauses.requirement: disclose AI tool usage, e.g. via an 'Assisted-by:' commit trailer
clauses.condition: where the contribution contains substantial amounts of tool-generated content
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs, coding assistants, AI agents and automated review tools used for LLVM contributions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Labelling is intended to facilitate reviews, not to track which parts of LLVM are generated.

clauses.original_text: An important implication of this policy is that it bans agents that take action in our digital spaces without human approval, such as the GitHub @claude agent. Similarly, automated review tools that publish comments without human review are not allowed.
clauses.object: AI agents acting without human approval; automated review tools publishing without human review
clauses.requirement: no autonomous AI agents or unreviewed automated review comments in project spaces
clauses.exception: opt-in review tools that keep a human in the loop
clauses.purpose: keep a human in the loop
clauses.applicable_systems: AI agents and automated review tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Opt-in review tools that keep a human in the loop are acceptable.

clauses.original_text: AI tools must not be used to fix GitHub issues labelled good first issue.
clauses.requirement: 'good first issue' tasks must be done without AI tools
clauses.purpose: preserve learning opportunities for new contributors
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI tool
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Restated in bold: 'Using AI tools to fix issues labelled as "good first issues" is forbidden'. Rationale is skill-building rather than output quality.

clauses.original_text: Contributors are responsible for ensuring that they have the right to contribute code under the terms of our license, typically meaning that either they, their employer, or their collaborators hold the copyright. Using AI tools to regenerate copyrighted material does not remove the copyright, and contributors are responsible for ensuring that such material does not appear in their contributions.
clauses.action: ensure rights to contribute; keep out
clauses.requirement: contributors ensure licensing rights and exclude copyrighted material reproduced by AI
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs, coding assistants, AI agents and automated review tools used for LLVM contributions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Contributions found to violate this are removed like any other offending contribution.

clauses.original_text: If a contributor fails to make their change meaningfully less extractive, maintainers should escalate to the relevant moderation or admin team for the space (GitHub, Discourse, Discord, etc) to lock the conversation.
clauses.requirement: escalate and lock conversations where contributors do not fix extractive contributions
clauses.condition: if the contributor fails to make the change meaningfully less extractive
clauses.purpose: enforce the policy and protect maintainer time
clauses.applicable_systems: contributions in GitHub, Discourse, Discord and other project spaces
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Preceded by a standard request-changes response and the 'extractive' label.

covered_entities: LSE academic staff (markers, second markers, moderators, teaching assistants)
covered_systems: GenAI tools (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
unsupported GenAI tools (only with rationale and consent)
exceptions: dissertations on taught programmes (excluded in the pilot year)
automated marking of objective formats (MCQs, online quizzes) predating GenAI

conditions: pilot year 2025/26, then review

documents.objective: Set principles and guidelines for responsible, transparent, human-led use of GenAI in marking, feedback and moderation at LSE, protecting students and trust while allowing safe experimentation.
principles: no AI detection of student AI use
documents.conflict_rule: Standard university regulations apply: where AI-assisted feedback has been appropriately used, challenges to academic judgement will not be accepted (s.3.1); LSE's moderation process is unchanged.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/lse-marking.pdf). The copy is the version 'revised post EC Nov 2025' with an executive summary (PDF dated 2 Dec 2025). Approved by Chair's Action on 7 Nov 2025 for a pilot year 2025/26, after which it is to be reviewed, so a later version may exist. Treated as an enforceable internal policy because its principles use 'must' and prohibit AI-generated marking, though the document also calls itself guidance and is neutral on whether staff use AI at all. No official LSE URL is printed in the document.

clauses.original_text: However, the use AI-generated marking and feedback, where AI systems independently generate marks and/or feedback with minimal or no human involvement is not permitted. The only exception to this prohibition is for automated marking of objective assessment formats such as multiple-choice questions (MCQs), online quizzes, or similar computer-marked assessments where automated marking has been an established practice predating GenAI tools.
clauses.object: AI-generated marking and feedback (minimal or no human involvement)
clauses.requirement: AI may not independently generate marks or feedback
clauses.exception: automated marking of objective formats (MCQs, online quizzes) established before GenAI
clauses.purpose: preserve human academic judgement and student trust
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Grammar ('the use AI-generated') as in source. Reinforced in s.3.1: AI 'cannot replace human academic judgment in determining marks, conducting moderation, or making final assessment decisions'.

clauses.original_text: Staff must clearly communicate to students when and how they use AI tools for marking and feedback
clauses.object: when and how AI tools are used for marking and feedback
clauses.requirement: disclose AI use in marking and feedback to students
clauses.condition: where AI tools are used in marking/feedback
clauses.purpose: transparency; preserve trust between staff and students
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: First principle ('Transparency first' in the executive summary). Bullet has no closing full stop in the source.

clauses.original_text: Staff must use LSE approved GenAI tools - such as Claude AI and Microsoft Copilot - for any AI-assisted activities related to assessment, including feedback, marking, and moderation. These tools are selected to ensure compliance with data protection regulations (e.g. UK GDPR), and offer enterprise-grade assurances around security, data integrity, privacy, and responsible AI use.
clauses.object: LSE-approved GenAI tools (Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.requirement: use only approved enterprise GenAI tools for assessment-related AI use
clauses.condition: for AI-assisted assessment activities
clauses.exception: s.4.1: if unsupported tools are used, staff should explain their rationale and obtain student and institutional consent
clauses.purpose: data protection, security and privacy of student work
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Section 4.1 softens this to 'should use institutionally approved GenAI tools' and allows unsupported tools with student and institutional consent, so the MUST is qualified.

clauses.original_text: Academic staff should not use GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI, as these tools are unreliable
clauses.object: GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI
clauses.requirement: do not use GenAI-based detection of student AI use
clauses.purpose: avoid unreliable detection leading to unfair outcomes
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used as AI-use detectors
clauses.interpretation_notes: Bullet has no closing full stop in the source.

clauses.original_text: Staff must not include student details or upload student work into GenAI tools without explicit permission. This prevents personal data from being collected, stored, accessed, and shared without consent.
clauses.requirement: no student details or work in GenAI tools without explicit permission
clauses.condition: without explicit permission
clauses.exception: with students' explicit permission
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: PDF line break inside 'shared / without consent' rejoined. Scenarios show staff using anonymised summaries instead of uploading student work.

clauses.original_text: Staff must provide human oversight at every stage of their approach. GenAI can generate incorrect responses based on probabilities and biases.
clauses.requirement: human oversight at every stage of AI-assisted marking and feedback
clauses.purpose: catch incorrect or biased AI outputs
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy and fairness of feedback and marks
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Companion guideline: 'Staff should ensure AI-assisted feedback does not independently determine marks or academic judgements.'

documents.objective: Make LSE staff and students aware of the legal and regulatory issues around AI use (competition and confidentiality, copyright, cybersecurity, data protection, equality) so that they do not breach the law when using AI.

related_policies.policy: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/lse-legreg.pdf). The document is labelled 'Operational' and version 2, approved by the AI Working Group on 24/10/2024 (PDF created Dec 2024); its next review was due 31/10/2025, so a newer version may exist. Classed as guidance/voluntary because it is framed as guidance, although it says it sets out 'the guidelines you must operate under' and breaches (e.g. of confidentiality) may lead to disciplinary sanctions. No official LSE URL is printed in the document. The legislation section (EU AI Act, UK AI Regulation Bill, TUC manifesto) reflects the position as at June 2024.

clauses.original_text: Don’t put personal data in an AI tool that is external to LSE. If it will swallow the personal data for further processing that LSE cannot control, you can’t use the AI tool.
clauses.requirement: do not enter personal data into external AI tools whose further processing LSE cannot control
clauses.condition: where the AI tool is external to LSE
clauses.purpose: UK GDPR compliance; prevent loss of control over personal data
clauses.affected_asset: personal data of staff, students and research subjects
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Phrased as a 'Don't' instruction in the guidance; repeated in the Cybersecurity AI rules ('do not ingest any personal data into AI tools') and Data Protection principles ('Do not share personal data with external AI tools').

clauses.original_text: Don’t upload in-copyright content (for example , images, photographs, student work, journal articles licensed from publishers by LSE library) where you do not have the copyright holder’s permission and where the AI tool is known to use inputs as training data.
clauses.object: in-copyright content (images, photographs, student work, licensed journal articles)
clauses.recipient: AI tools that use inputs as training data
clauses.requirement: do not upload copyrighted material without permission to tools that train on inputs
clauses.condition: where the copyright holder has not given permission and the tool is known to train on inputs
clauses.purpose: avoid copyright infringement and breach of library licences
clauses.affected_asset: third-party copyright works; LSE library licences
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Stray space before the comma ('for example , images') is in the source. The Copyright section adds that MS Copilot may be used to summarise copyrighted work and that the TDM exception (s.29A CDPA) covers only non-commercial research.

clauses.original_text: Conduct an Equality Impact Assessment if there is a chance of data leading to bias or discrimination.
clauses.actor: LSE staff and students using AI
clauses.requirement: carry out an EIA where AI use could lead to bias or discrimination
clauses.condition: if there is a chance of data leading to bias or discrimination
clauses.purpose: comply with the Equality Act 2010; prevent discrimination on protected characteristics
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Listed under 'Do'; imperative but the document is guidance. The Equality Act section elaborates (profiling, automated decision-making, EIAs).

clauses.original_text: Remember that you're always accountable for any decisions you make, so be very wary of making decisions solely based on AI outputs. Any automated decisions that have real-world impacts on humans must allow for a human review.
clauses.object: automated decisions with real-world impacts on humans
clauses.requirement: automated decisions affecting people must allow human review; users remain accountable for decisions
clauses.condition: where automated decisions have real-world impacts on humans
clauses.purpose: accountability; UK GDPR Article 22 safeguards against solely automated decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Linked to the Data Protection section's discussion of UK GDPR Article 22 (e.g. students told if AI is used for marking and able to request human review).

clauses.original_text: Do not trust any information supplied by AI tools without undertaking independent verification. AI tools are known to hallucinate, namely supplying information that has no basis in reality, or else reproducing information that is out of date or is misinformation.
clauses.requirement: do not rely on AI-supplied information without independent verification
clauses.purpose: avoid reliance on hallucinated, outdated or false information
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy of work products and decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Sub-point (a) merged into the quote.

clauses.original_text: Never ask an AI to perform tasks that are malicious or that may compromise other people or data that is not yours. This at a minimum would constitute a breach of the Computer Misuse Act 1990, the Terms of Use of Jisc’s network, our M365 tenancy agreement and the standard terms of most AI tool providers.
clauses.object: malicious tasks or tasks compromising other people or their data
clauses.requirement: no malicious use of AI or use that compromises others' systems or data
clauses.purpose: prevent computer misuse and harm to third parties
clauses.affected_asset: other people; third-party data and systems
clauses.applicable_systems: AI tools used by LSE staff and students (generative and predictive; MS Copilot, public and external AI)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Echoes 'Don't ask an AI tool to do something malicious or illegal' under 'What not to do'.

covered_entities: anyone given access to the Force IT environment

UK Government Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI

documents.conflict_rule: Use must comply with the Code of Ethics, data protection law and the Force's wider policies; the SIRO (Deputy Chief Constable) may revoke any AI use at any time.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/leicestershire_police.md). The asago copy is a Markdown conversion of the force document (tables as HTML, some list bullets lost, '100%' rendered as LaTeX). Annex A (governance process for new AI tools), referenced in §4.3, is not in the copy. Only the creation entry (21/10/2025) appears in the review log; the next review date is 01/05/2026, so a revised version may now exist (not checked). Numbering in §5.3 is duplicated in the original ('3.' and '6.' appear twice). Binding=false (not law); adherence is mandatory for all officers, staff, volunteers, contractors and others with access to the Force IT environment (§2).

clauses.original_text: As of the date of this document, the following represent the only standalone AI applications authorised for use by Leicestershire Police personnel: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (Free Version); Microsoft 365 Copilot (Licensed Version). No other standalone AI tools may be used within the Force.
clauses.requirement: only Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat / Copilot; consumer tools (ChatGPT, Deepseek, Gemini, Perplexity, self-hosted LLMs) prohibited
clauses.exception: new standalone tools approved by the Artificial Intelligence Board (§4.3)
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Bullet list flattened with semicolons (full stop added after the list). §5.3 item 2 adds: use a force account on a force device; personal accounts/devices prohibited.

clauses.original_text: However, due to the nature of policing and the critical importance of safeguarding sensitive operations, the following types of information must never be entered, pasted, uploaded, or otherwise submitted into Microsoft's Co-pilot or any other AI tool—regardless of the device or platform: Any data marked or implicitly classified as SECRET or TOP SECRET. … Covert Human Intelligence Sources (CHIS) Related Information …
clauses.object: SECRET/TOP SECRET data, CHIS information, information under handling conditions, legally privileged information, sensitive operational data, system credentials
clauses.requirement: never submit prohibited information types into any AI tool
clauses.exception: OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE (incl. personal data) permitted in risk-assessed, authorised tools
clauses.purpose: safeguard sensitive operations and national security
clauses.affected_asset: classified and operational police information; CHIS identities
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Other listed types elided with '…'. Guiding principle: if unsure, do not input it.

clauses.section: 5.3 What should I consider when using AI? – 4. Check the results
clauses.original_text: Check the results – AI is not 100% reliable and you must always read and verify anything produced.
clauses.requirement: verify AI outputs
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy of police records and decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: '100%' appears as LaTeX '$100\%$' in the Markdown copy (conversion artefact fixed).

clauses.section: 5.3 What should I consider when using AI? – 5. Be transparent
clauses.original_text: Be transparent – Don't claim AI produced work as your own. Although there is no need to declare every use of AI such as for note taking, drafting work you heavily edit or for research, transparency is essential to maintain the public trust so always declare the use of AI in any formal report, creative content or when it is used in decision making.
clauses.object: formal reports, creative content, AI-supported decisions
clauses.requirement: declare AI use in formal reports, creative content and decision-making
clauses.condition: formal reports, creative content or decision making
clauses.exception: note taking, heavily edited drafts and research need not be declared
clauses.affected_asset: public trust; integrity of police outputs
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Suggested note: 'Microsoft Copilot supported the creation of this document'.

clauses.section: 5.3 What should I consider when using AI? – 6. Human Review
clauses.original_text: Human Review - AI must not be allowed to make operational decisions without human review. AI can be used as a tool, to present options and wider considerations. However, the responsibility and liability remain with the police decision maker. AI can never be used as a defence or rationale for a poor decision.
clauses.requirement: no operational decisions by AI without human review; liability stays with the decision maker
clauses.affected_asset: rights of the public; police legitimacy
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)

clauses.section: 5.4 AI use in the Criminal Justice System
clauses.original_text: The use of AI technologies is not yet authorised for use in the Criminal Justice process, including for the creation of evidential materials. This means it must not be used in the preparation of witness statements, MG forms, or any other court ready evidential reports.
clauses.object: witness statements, MG forms, court-ready evidential reports
clauses.requirement: no AI in creating evidential material
clauses.exception: AI MG form generation in the approved force trial with East Midlands CPS using GoodSAM AI
clauses.purpose: integrity of evidence and fair trial
clauses.affected_asset: criminal justice process; defendants and witnesses
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: AI may support investigators in understanding evidence if it does not generate official evidential documentation.

clauses.section: 3.0 We will not use AI in ways that harm people or put them or their rights at risk.
clauses.original_text: Lenovo prohibits AI systems that: (a) deploy subliminal or manipulative techniques, (b) exploit a person’s vulnerabilities, (c) discriminatorily classify people based on their social behavior, socio-economic status, or sensitive personal information such as race or ethnicity, (d) use or were trained on biometric data indiscriminately scraped from social media or publicly-available information, or (e) involve the collection of sensitive personal data to enable profiling of individuals.
clauses.object: manipulative, exploitative, discriminatory-classification, scraped-biometric and sensitive-profiling AI systems
clauses.requirement: no development, acquisition or use of the listed AI systems
clauses.purpose: protect people and their rights from harmful AI
clauses.affected_asset: natural persons; their rights and personal data
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system developed, acquired, incorporated or used by Lenovo
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (lenovo.pdf); line breaks collapsed. The list mirrors several EU AI Act Article 5 prohibited practices without citing the Act.

clauses.original_text: In determining whether to develop, use, or implement an AI system, Lenovo will evaluate it (e.g., data sets, algorithms, user interfaces) to ensure the AI system mitigates bias and ensures fair and equal treatment for all users.
clauses.object: AI systems (data sets, algorithms, user interfaces)

clauses.original_text: More specifically, users should be: (a) informed that they are interacting with AI, (b) provided with information about how their data will be handled by the AI, (c) informed of any choices they can make regarding their interactions with AI, and (d) made aware of any rights they may have to challenge an AI-generated outcome.

clauses.purpose: ensure validity, fairness and accountability of AI outcomes

clauses.original_text: Importantly, this means that our employees may not use publicly-available versions of any generative AI tool – like ChatGPT, Midjourney, and many others – for work purposes. Only AI tools specifically licensed and approved by Lenovo may be used.
