clauses.original_text: 1. CBRN Information or Capabilities: Eased access to or synthesis of materially nefarious information or design capabilities related to chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) weapons or other dangerous materials or agents.
clauses.object: CBRN information or capabilities risk from GAI
clauses.requirement: treat eased access to CBRN weapon information/design capabilities as a GAI risk category to be managed
clauses.purpose: prevent GAI uplift to chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Definitional clause from the 12-risk taxonomy; modality is notional (the profile uses the taxonomy to scope suggested actions).

clauses.original_text: Establish minimum thresholds for performance or assurance criteria and review as part of deployment approval (“go/”no-go”) policies, procedures, and processes, with reviewed processes and approval thresholds reflecting measurement of GAI capabilities and risks.
clauses.object: minimum performance/assurance thresholds in go/no-go deployment approval
clauses.requirement: set deployment approval thresholds tied to measured GAI capabilities and risks
clauses.condition: as part of deployment approval
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mapped in the profile to CBRN; Confabulation; Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content. Quotation marks around go/no-go reproduced as in source.

clauses.original_text: Establish a test plan and response policy, before developing highly capable models, to periodically evaluate whether the model may misuse CBRN information or capabilities and/or offensive cyber capabilities.
clauses.actor: developer of highly capable GAI models
clauses.action: establish test plan and response policy; periodically evaluate
clauses.object: model potential to misuse CBRN or offensive cyber capabilities
clauses.requirement: plan and periodically run dangerous-capability evaluations with a response policy
clauses.condition: before developing highly capable models
clauses.purpose: detect and respond to dangerous CBRN/cyber capabilities
clauses.applicable_systems: highly capable generative AI models
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'Highly capable models' is not defined in the profile.

clauses.original_text: Apply established security measures to: Assess likelihood and magnitude of vulnerabilities and threats such as backdoors, compromised dependencies, data breaches, eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, reverse engineering, autonomous agents, model theft or exposure of model weights, AI inference, bypass, extraction, and other baseline security concerns.
clauses.action: apply security measures and assess vulnerabilities and threats
clauses.requirement: assess likelihood/magnitude of listed security threats including model-weight theft
clauses.purpose: security and resilience of GAI systems
clauses.affected_asset: model weights, training data, system integrity
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mapped to Data Privacy; Information Integrity; Information Security; Value Chain and Component Integration.

clauses.original_text: Establish and regularly review specific criteria that warrants the deactivation of GAI systems in accordance with set risk tolerances and appetites.
clauses.action: establish and regularly review deactivation criteria
clauses.requirement: define and review criteria for deactivating GAI systems
clauses.condition: in accordance with organizational risk tolerances and appetites
clauses.purpose: enable timely shutdown of harmful GAI systems
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Grammar ('criteria that warrants') reproduced as in source.

clauses.original_text: Report GAI incidents in compliance with legal and regulatory requirements (e.g., HIPAA breach reporting, e.g., OCR (2023) or NHTSA (2022) autonomous vehicle crash reporting requirements.
clauses.requirement: report GAI incidents as required by applicable law
clauses.condition: where legal or regulatory reporting requirements apply
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Unbalanced parenthesis is in the source. The profile does not itself create a reporting duty; it points to existing legal duties.

clauses.original_text: GOVERN 1.1: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
clauses.object: legal and regulatory requirements involving AI
clauses.requirement: identify, manage and document applicable AI legal and regulatory requirements
clauses.purpose: legal compliance as a foundation of AI risk governance
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Framework outcomes are phrased as states ('are understood') rather than imperatives; modality SHOULD reflects the voluntary nature.

clauses.original_text: GOVERN 4.1: Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.
clauses.action: put in place policies and practices
clauses.requirement: establish policies fostering a safety-first mindset across the AI lifecycle
clauses.purpose: minimize potential negative impacts of AI systems
clauses.affected_asset: people and organizations affected by AI systems
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Cultural/organizational outcome; measurable evidence is left to the Playbook's suggested actions.

clauses.original_text: GOVERN 6.1: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party’s intellectual property or other rights.
clauses.object: AI risks from third-party entities (software, data, supply chain)
clauses.requirement: address third-party and supply-chain AI risks, including IP infringement
clauses.purpose: manage supply-chain and third-party rights risks
clauses.affected_asset: third-party intellectual property and other rights; organizational systems
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems using third-party software, data or models
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from Table 1; GOVERN 6.2 (contingency processes for third-party failures) is the companion outcome.

clauses.original_text: MEASURE 2.6: The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks – as identified in the MAP function. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics reflect system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.
clauses.requirement: regularly evaluate safety; demonstrate residual risk within tolerance and safe failure before deployment
clauses.condition: before deployment and on a regular basis thereafter
clauses.purpose: ensure AI systems are safe and fail safely
clauses.affected_asset: human life, health, property and the environment
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system to be deployed
clauses.interpretation_notes: Combines a recurring evaluation outcome with a pre-deployment demonstration; 'risk tolerance' is organization-defined (GOVERN 1.3).

clauses.original_text: MANAGE 1.1: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
clauses.requirement: make a documented go/no-go decision based on whether the system meets its intended purpose
clauses.condition: based on outputs of the MAP and MEASURE functions
clauses.purpose: avoid developing or deploying systems that do not meet objectives or carry unacceptable risk
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Commonly read as the framework's explicit go/no-go gate.

clauses.original_text: MANAGE 2.4: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
clauses.action: establish mechanisms and assign responsibility to supersede, disengage or deactivate
clauses.object: AI systems behaving inconsistently with intended use
clauses.requirement: maintain working shutdown/override mechanisms with assigned owners
clauses.condition: when performance or outcomes are inconsistent with intended use
clauses.purpose: contain harm from malfunctioning or misused AI
clauses.applicable_systems: any deployed AI system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Often called the 'kill switch' subcategory in secondary literature.

clauses.original_text: Principle B. Transparent: All use of AI will be subject to ‘Maximum Transparency by Default’ (MTbD). B1. Forces should ensure the public are aware of AI uses. This will typically include publishing an overview of the algorithms used and the known limitations of the training data used.

clauses.original_text: Principle C. Explainable: The ability for any AI to provide an ‘explanation’ of its output will be a determining factor in its implementation.
clauses.requirement: explainability determines whether AI is implemented

clauses.original_text: Principle D. Responsible: All AI that affects the public will have responsible usage policies (i.e., intensions are defined before deployment so that outcomes and impact can be tracked) and procedures to ensure that users do not accept AI outputs uncritically. … D2. All AI that effects the public must have a human as the ultimate decision-maker.

clauses.requirement: human ultimate decision-maker; usage policies against uncritical acceptance of outputs
clauses.condition: AI affects the public
clauses.affected_asset: rights of members of the public
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing

clauses.original_text: D3. All AI will have a human or automatic means of being stopped if it displays unintended or undesired outputs.
clauses.requirement: human or automatic means to stop AI

clauses.interpretation_notes: Phrased with 'will'.

clauses.original_text: D4. Those responsible for AI-enabled systems must proactively mitigate the risk of unintended biases or harms, during initial rollout and as they learn, change, or are redeployed.
clauses.requirement: proactive bias/harm mitigation across the lifecycle
clauses.condition: at rollout and as systems learn, change or are redeployed

clauses.original_text: SEs must ensure that decisions that impact the public are not made without oversight by appropriate staff, who make the final decisions. Automated final decision systems are not permitted.
clauses.action: ensure human oversight and final decision by staff

clauses.condition: decisions that impact the public
clauses.purpose: protect the public from unchecked automated decisions
clauses.affected_asset: rights, safety and welfare of the public
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public

clauses.original_text: Use of AI systems must be fair and equitable in accordance with applicable State and Federal laws, rules, and regulations. SE must be aware that systemic, computational, and human biases may impact AI systems and should develop a plan to monitor for such biases, and, where identified, remediated identified biases.

clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: Fairness itself is MUST; the bias monitoring plan is phrased SHOULD. Wording 'remediated' is as in the document.

clauses.original_text: Where members of the public interact directly with SE systems that use AI technology, the use of such AI technology should be disclosed by the SE. Furthermore, SE users of AI systems must provide meaningful oversight over all decisions made by an AI system and be able to explain the decision or output.

clauses.requirement: disclose AI interaction to the public; be able to explain AI decisions
clauses.condition: where the public interacts directly with an AI-enabled SE system
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: Footnote marker 6 omitted. Disclosure is SHOULD; explainability/oversight is MUST. Footnote 6 example: chatbot users should be made aware they are interacting with a machine.

clauses.original_text: The SE must perform a Risk Assessment for each AI system that meets the criteria set forth in Section 3.2. The Risk Assessment must include a review of all security, privacy, legal, reputational, and competency risks as well as the additional risks listed in this policy.

clauses.section: Principle 1.2 (Respect for the rule of law, human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy)
clauses.original_text: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights, democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI system lifecycle. These include non-discrimination and equality, freedom, dignity, autonomy of individuals, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice, and internationally recognised labour rights. … To this end, AI actors should implement mechanisms and safeguards, such as capacity for human agency and oversight, including to address risks arising from uses outside of intended purpose, intentional misuse, or unintentional misuse in a manner appropriate to the context and consistent with the state of the art.
clauses.requirement: respect rule of law, human rights and democratic values; implement human agency and oversight safeguards
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Not verbatim-verified: the official host (legalinstruments.oecd.org) was not reachable from the compilation environment (network policy), so this wording is the compiler's reconstruction of the official text and must be checked against the official source before being treated as a quotation.

clauses.original_text: AI Actors should commit to transparency and responsible disclosure regarding AI systems. To this end, they should provide meaningful information, appropriate to the context, and consistent with the state of art: … to make stakeholders aware of their interactions with AI systems, including in the workplace, … where feasible and useful, to provide plain and easy-to-understand information on the sources of data/input, factors, processes and/or logic that led to the prediction, content, recommendation or decision, to enable those affected by an AI system to understand the output, and, to provide information that enable those adversely affected by an AI system to challenge its output.
clauses.requirement: disclose AI interactions and explain outputs to enable understanding and challenge
clauses.condition: appropriate to context and consistent with state of the art; where feasible and useful
clauses.affected_asset: affected persons' ability to understand and challenge AI outputs
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Not verbatim-verified: the official host (legalinstruments.oecd.org) was not reachable from the compilation environment (network policy), so this wording is the compiler's reconstruction of the official text and must be checked against the official source before being treated as a quotation.

clauses.original_text: a) AI systems should be robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle so that, in conditions of normal use, foreseeable use or misuse, or other adverse conditions, they function appropriately and do not pose unreasonable safety and/or security risks. b) Mechanisms should be in place, as appropriate, to ensure that if AI systems risk causing undue harm or exhibit undesired behaviour, they can be overridden, repaired, and/or decommissioned safely as needed. c) Mechanisms should also, where technically feasible, be in place to bolster information integrity while ensuring respect for freedom of expression.
clauses.requirement: ensure robustness, security and safety; enable safe override, repair or decommissioning; bolster information integrity
clauses.condition: throughout lifecycle, incl. normal use, foreseeable use or misuse
clauses.purpose: prevent unreasonable safety/security risks and undue harm
clauses.affected_asset: safety and security of people; information integrity
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Not verbatim-verified: the official host (legalinstruments.oecd.org) was not reachable from the compilation environment (network policy), so this wording is the compiler's reconstruction of the official text and must be checked against the official source before being treated as a quotation. Points (b) and (c) were added in the 2024 revision.

clauses.original_text: Undertake privacy impact assessments (PIAs) to understand the ways in which the enterprise Generative AI tool will be utilised, the risks it presents to the privacy of individuals, whether and how those risks can be mitigated, and in light of any residual risks, the extent to which it is appropriate to proceed to purchase the tool.

clauses.condition: prior to purchasing and integrating an enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.purpose: protect individuals' privacy; decide whether to proceed
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. Footnote 7: one overarching PIA is likely insufficient; PIAs should be per function or business unit.

clauses.original_text: Ensure that enterprise Generative AI tools are not used to make decisions, undertake assessments, or for other administrative functions that may have consequences for individuals or cause them significant harm.
clauses.object: enterprise Generative AI tools for consequential decisions or assessments
clauses.requirement: prevent use of enterprise Generative AI to make decisions or assessments with consequences for individuals
clauses.purpose: avoid unfair decisions based on inaccurate or diminished-quality AI-generated information
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed.

clauses.original_text: Ensure that settings can be configured to enhance information privacy and information security, such as disabling or limiting data sharing between certain platforms and between the VPS organisation and the company that owns the enterprise Generative AI tool.
clauses.object: data sharing settings of enterprise Generative AI tools
clauses.requirement: configure the tool to limit data sharing between platforms and with the vendor
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed.

clauses.original_text: Develop and implement clear and tailored guidance and training for their staff, contracted service providers and other personnel on the use of the enterprise Generative AI tool, that: covers how to safely and responsibly use the enterprise Generative AI tool, prompt engineering, risk assessment and management, human review of generated outputs, and active monitoring and reviews to identify potential misuse ensures all users of the enterprise Generative AI tool are aware of and understand what information they are permitted to enter into the enterprise Generative AI tool and its permitted use cases
clauses.object: use of the enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.recipient: staff, contracted service providers and other personnel
clauses.requirement: train users on safe use, human review of outputs, permitted inputs and permitted use cases
clauses.purpose: safe and responsible use; prevent misuse and inaccurate outputs
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. Nested bullets flattened; a third bullet (awareness of how the tool handles personal information and ensuring accuracy) omitted.

clauses.original_text: Develop an incident response plan for dealing with inadvertent or unauthorised disclosures, access or misuse of information through the enterprise Generative AI tool. VPS organisations are responsible for all actions and content generated by the enterprise Generative AI tool they use. Where an information security incident or interference with privacy occurs through the use of the tool, VPS organisations will not be able to simply say that the incident or interference was caused by AI. Notify OVIC of information privacy and information security incidents, in line with the Information Security Incident Notification Scheme.
clauses.object: information privacy and security incidents involving the tool
clauses.requirement: maintain an AI incident response plan, accept responsibility for AI-generated content and notify OVIC of incidents
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the .docx (pandoc text); footnote markers removed. Two consecutive bullets combined.

clauses.original_text: Before VPS organisations implement any enterprise Generative AI tool, the public sector body head must assess the information security risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of public sector information and systems proposed to be used by the enterprise Generative AI tool, and ensure adherence to the Victorian Protective Data Security Standards (the Standards).
clauses.object: information security risks of the enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.recipient: contracted service providers (via the security risk assessment)
clauses.requirement: assess confidentiality, integrity and availability risks and comply with the VPDSS before implementation, including evaluation of relevant contracted service providers
clauses.condition: before implementing any enterprise Generative AI tool
clauses.purpose: protect public sector information and systems
clauses.applicable_systems: enterprise Generative AI tools (e.g. tenanted Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)

clauses.section: Tracked Categories (Biological and Chemical; Cybersecurity; AI Self-improvement)
clauses.original_text: OpenAI tracks three frontier capability categories it treats as plausible, measurable, severe, net-new and instantaneous-or-irremediable risks: Biological and Chemical, Cybersecurity, and AI Self-improvement, each with High and Critical capability thresholds; further areas (e.g., long-range autonomy, sandbagging, autonomous replication and adaptation, undermining safeguards, nuclear and radiological) are Research Categories.

clauses.requirement: evaluate covered models against High and Critical thresholds in each Tracked Category

clauses.requirement: route deployment/development decisions for covered models through SAG review, leadership decision and board-committee oversight

clauses.original_text: Agencies shall ensure that AI solutions have appropriate interventions and checks from humans, otherwise known as human in the loop (HITL) procedures, meaning there is active human participation in the decision-making process, review, oversight, and validation of AI systems including any generated content or output.
clauses.object: human-in-the-loop interventions and checks on AI solutions
clauses.requirement: HITL procedures for AI decision-making, review, oversight and validation
clauses.condition: before agencies begin an AI initiative (key consideration)
clauses.purpose: maintain human control over AI-assisted decisions and outputs
clauses.affected_asset: Commonwealth decisions; citizens and employees affected
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions and generative AI tools used by Commonwealth agencies
clauses.interpretation_notes: Listed among key considerations agencies 'shall evaluate' before starting an AI initiative.

clauses.original_text: Evaluate the level of risk that AI systems are exploited by malicious actors and determine appropriate risk controls. Establish controls to prevent adversarial learning to include attacks that try to influence the training data of spam filters or systems for abnormal network traffic detection, designed to mislead the learning algorithm for subsequent exploitation.
clauses.object: exploitation of AI systems and adversarial learning
clauses.requirement: assess exploitation risk and implement controls against adversarial attacks
clauses.purpose: secure AI systems against malicious actors
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions and generative AI tools used by Commonwealth agencies
clauses.interpretation_notes: Introduced by 'the following shall be considered for use', so modality recorded as SHOULD. Bullets joined.

clauses.original_text: When using any Generative AI for Commonwealth business purposes, the user is accountable for any Generative AI outputs and must review and verify all associated output content.
clauses.requirement: users are accountable for and must verify all GenAI output
clauses.condition: when using GenAI for Commonwealth business purposes
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: The section adds that users must have experience in the relevant topic area to verify outputs, and lists bias, dated or inaccurate information, hallucinations, inappropriate content, IP and confidential information as review points.

clauses.original_text: Users shall be transparent about their use of generative AI and must disclose to customers, residents, visitors, and industry when generative AI has been used to generate content that may be public facing or shared externally. Generative AI use must be disclosed even if it was only used to generate a portion of the content. The disclosure shall be prominently displayed and include an indication that the content was generated either entirely or in part by generative AI and identify the Generative AI system and version that was used.
clauses.object: use of generative AI in public-facing or externally shared content
clauses.requirement: prominent disclosure naming the GenAI system and version
clauses.condition: content that may be public facing or shared externally
clauses.affected_asset: public trust; recipients of Commonwealth content
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Example given: 'ChatGPT-3.5 was used in the creation of this document.' Section 5.1.5 separately requires AI solutions to disclose to customers that they are interacting with AI.

clauses.original_text: No class C data, as defined in the Data Classification Policy, may be input into any generative AI prompt, tool, or system. This includes, but is not limited to: Sensitive Security Information; Personal Identifiable Information (PII); Protected Health Information (PHI); … Confidential or Non-Public Information; Privileged Information; Prerequisite-Required Information
clauses.object: class C data (SSI, PII, PHI, regulated, confidential, privileged data)
clauses.recipient: generative AI prompts, tools or systems
clauses.requirement: no class C data in any generative AI tool
clauses.purpose: protect sensitive, personal and regulated data
clauses.affected_asset: personal data; PHI; regulated data (SSA, IRS, CMS, CJI, CHRIA, FERPA, PCI DSS)
clauses.applicable_systems: any generative AI prompt, tool, or system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Bulleted list flattened with semicolons; the regulated-data sub-list is elided. Non-public records exempt under the Right-to-Know Law (65 P.S. §§ 67.101 et seq.) are also excluded.

clauses.original_text: Generative AI outputs are not to be used to make decisions for or on behalf of employees. Employees may use generative AI outputs to inform a larger decision-making process, but ultimately the Commonwealth employee or official remains the final decision maker. … Generative AI cannot make reliable subjective or value-based judgments and may not be used for such purposes.
clauses.action: not use GenAI outputs to make
clauses.requirement: GenAI informs but never makes decisions; a human remains the final decision maker
clauses.exception: GenAI outputs may inform a larger human decision-making process
clauses.affected_asset: employees and citizens affected by decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Example in source: 'do not use generative AI to make final decisions that affect employment.'

clauses.section: Red Lines – SAP Red Line Cases
clauses.original_text: No SAP AI use cases should fall under the so-called Red Lines defined in the SAP AI Ethics Policy. These are defined as highly unethical under the purposes for AI. If your use case is built for these purposes, you are required to immediately stop developing, deploying, and selling that use case.

Red lines listed alongside: human surveillance targeting individuals or groups (biometrics, facial recognition) to disregard or abuse their rights; discriminatory purposes; deanonymization of anonymized data; manipulation for deception; systems undermining human debate or democratic electoral systems; environmental harm; intentionally harmful impacts.

clauses.section: High Risk – SAP High Risk Cases

clauses.original_text: AI systems shall be subject to appropriate human oversight, and the rights and freedoms of a human shall exceed that of AI systems. In situations where humans may be directly impacted by a decision made by SAP’s AI system, human oversight shall be introduced to safeguard that AI system does not undermine human autonomy or introduce unintended consequences.

AI systems shall clearly signal to end users that its social interaction is simulated.

clauses.affected_asset: groups and individuals affected by AI outputs

documents.objective: Establish a proportionate, context-specific and pro-innovation framework in which existing regulators apply five cross-sectoral principles to AI within their remits, supported by central government functions, rather than creating a new AI-specific regulator or horizontal AI law.

related_policies.note: divergent regulatory approach (sector-led principles vs horizontal statute), not a legal conflict

documents.conflict_rule: Principles are applied 'in accordance with existing laws and regulations' (para. 50) and complement existing regulation; existing statutory duties (data protection, equality, consumer, sectoral law) prevail. 'conflicts_with' for the EU AI Act denotes a divergent regulatory philosophy (sectoral non-statutory vs horizontal statute), not a legal conflict.

sources_consulted: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-regulation-a-pro-innovation-approach (HTML text obtained via the Hugging Face dataset AndreasThinks/ukgov-policy-docs, a scrape of gov.uk policy papers)
record_provenance.notes: gov.uk could not be fetched directly in this session; clause text is taken from a third-party scrape of the gov.uk HTML version of CP 815 and should be re-checked against gov.uk. The February 2024 government response (CP 1019) text was not obtained; facts about it come from search results. As of Nov 2026 the UK has no AI-specific statute: the 2024 King's Speech commitment to legislate on the most powerful models has not resulted in a bill, and the May 2026 King's Speech (per law-firm and IAPP summaries) contained no standalone AI bill but announced a 'Regulating for Growth Bill' with AI Growth Lab sandbox powers — its introduction/stage could not be verified. The anticipated statutory 'due regard' duty on regulators has not been enacted. The white paper has not been formally withdrawn, but its status under the post-July-2024 government is best described as the existing non-statutory framework with policy emphasis shifted to the AI Opportunities Action Plan; 'voluntary' status reflects that it binds no one. Exact day of the July 2024 King's Speech (17 July) and the AI Opportunities Action Plan (13 January 2025) are from general knowledge.

clauses.original_text: 48. Existing regulators will be expected to implement the framework underpinned by 5 values-focused cross-sectoral principles: Safety, security and robustness Appropriate transparency and explainability Fairness Accountability and governance Contestability and redress

clauses.section: Section III.2 Principles - Proportionality and Do No Harm
clauses.original_text: The choice to use AI systems and which AI method to use should be justified: the method should be appropriate and proportional to achieve a legitimate aim, should not infringe human rights, and should be appropriate to the context. Where decisions may have irreversible or difficult-to-reverse impacts or involve life and death, final human determination should apply. AI systems in particular should not be used for social scoring or mass surveillance purposes.

clauses.requirement: AI systems perform reliably with minimal hallucination, ensured by testing and refinement
clauses.applicable_systems: eBay AI systems (internal-facing and customer-facing), across the lifecycle
clauses.interpretation_notes: Section continues with regular safety assessments to identify and rectify issues.

clauses.original_text: eBay’s AI systems should be secure and protected from unauthorized access, tampering, and any other form of malicious intervention, in accordance with eBay’s Information Security Policy and Standards.
clauses.requirement: protect AI systems from unauthorised access, tampering and malicious intervention
clauses.affected_asset: AI systems; eBay and user data
clauses.applicable_systems: eBay AI systems (internal-facing and customer-facing), across the lifecycle
clauses.interpretation_notes: Implemented through eBay's Information Security Policy and Standards (not included).

clauses.original_text: In particular, AI decisions must not discriminate based on age, gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, or any other protected characteristic. To ensure fairness, we must build AI systems with fairness and bias issues in mind, test and monitor AI systems regularly and give users the ability to give us feedback.
clauses.requirement: no discrimination on protected characteristics; regular fairness testing/monitoring and user feedback
clauses.applicable_systems: eBay AI systems (internal-facing and customer-facing), across the lifecycle
clauses.interpretation_notes: Combines a prohibition (no discrimination) with positive duties (MUST build/test/monitor, feedback channel).

clauses.original_text: In particular, human oversight should be integrated throughout the development, launch, and monitoring of AI systems. Throughout this lifecycle, decision-making should be informed by the level of risk and potential impact associated with the use case at hand.
clauses.object: AI system development, launch and monitoring
clauses.requirement: risk-proportionate human oversight across the AI lifecycle
clauses.applicable_systems: eBay AI systems (internal-facing and customer-facing), across the lifecycle
clauses.interpretation_notes: Section also requires documenting development, deployment and oversight decisions.

clauses.original_text: To the extent personal information is involved, eBay’s Privacy principles—which are the backbone of eBay’s Privacy program—should guide choices for AI system design, development, deployment, and use. This includes following a Privacy by Design approach, data minimization, data quality, and purpose specification.
clauses.requirement: privacy by design, data minimisation, data quality and purpose specification
clauses.condition: to the extent personal information is involved
clauses.affected_asset: personal data of users and employees
clauses.applicable_systems: eBay AI systems (internal-facing and customer-facing), across the lifecycle
clauses.interpretation_notes: eBay's Privacy principles themselves are not included in the document.

clauses.original_text: eBay should be transparent to users about its use of AI. We will promote transparency with disclosures about the type of AI being used within a particular experience or broader disclosures about our AI use more generally.
clauses.object: use of AI in eBay experiences
clauses.requirement: disclose AI use to users, specifically or generally, tailored to their needs
clauses.applicable_systems: eBay AI systems (internal-facing and customer-facing), across the lifecycle
clauses.interpretation_notes: Disclosure may be experience-specific or general; tailored to users' roles and understanding.

sources_consulted: Câmara open-data API /api/v2/proposicoes/2487262, via the GitHub mirror https://github.com/misspaiva/radar-pl-2338 (STATUS.md and data/historico-tramitacao.json, auto-generated 2026-11-09)
record_provenance.notes: camara.leg.br and senado.leg.br could not be fetched from this session, so the official bill text was NOT accessed. All clauses are Portuguese paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false) with unofficial English translations; article numbers (Art. 12 preliminary assessment, Art. 13 excessive risk, Art. 14 high risk, Art. 25 algorithmic impact assessment) follow the Câmara avulso of the Senate-approved text as surfaced in search excerpts, but secondary sources number some provisions differently — verify before citing. No official English translation exists. Procedural dates from 2025-03-17 onward are taken from the Câmara open-data history (via a GitHub mirror that republishes the API). Introduction date (3 May 2023) and Senate rapporteur from general knowledge. Sanction ceiling (R$ 50 million per infraction or 2% of gross revenue) reported by Agência Senado-derived summaries; the revenue base (group/conglomerate in Brazil) and article number not verified. Exceptions list is from general knowledge of the Senate text and needs verification.

clauses.original_text: [Paráfrase — não é o texto oficial] São vedados o desenvolvimento, a implementação e o uso de sistemas de IA de risco excessivo, entre eles: sistemas que empreguem técnicas subliminares ou explorem vulnerabilidades para induzir comportamento danoso; sistemas de pontuação social pelo poder público que restrinjam ilegítima ou desproporcionalmente o acesso a bens, serviços e políticas públicas; sistemas que avaliem traços de personalidade ou comportamento passado para prever o risco de cometimento de crimes; sistemas de armas autônomas; e sistemas que possibilitem a produção ou disseminação de material de abuso ou exploração sexual de crianças e adolescentes; com regras específicas e exceções para identificação biométrica à distância, em tempo real, em espaços acessíveis ao público.
clauses.translated_text: [Unofficial translation of paraphrase] The development, deployment and use of excessive-risk AI systems are prohibited, including: systems using subliminal techniques or exploiting vulnerabilities to induce harmful behaviour; social scoring by public authorities that illegitimately or disproportionately restricts access to goods, services and public policies; systems assessing personality traits or past behaviour to predict the risk of committing crimes; autonomous weapons systems; and systems enabling the production or dissemination of child sexual abuse or exploitation material; with specific rules and exceptions for real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces.
clauses.actor: AI agents (developers, distributors, deployers), including public authorities
clauses.requirement: do not develop, deploy or use the listed excessive-risk AI applications
clauses.condition: system falls within an excessive-risk category
clauses.exception: real-time remote biometric identification permitted in limited cases (e.g. specific public-security / criminal investigation scenarios) under conditions set in the text
clauses.purpose: protect fundamental rights, safety and children
clauses.affected_asset: human dignity, autonomy, equality, life and physical integrity, children
clauses.applicable_systems: excessive-risk AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase reconstructed from search excerpts of the Câmara avulso and secondary summaries; enumeration order and exact scope of each item not verified. Not law.

clauses.original_text: [Paráfrase — não é o texto oficial] Antes de sua introdução e circulação no mercado, emprego ou utilização, o agente de IA poderá realizar avaliação preliminar para determinar o grau de risco do sistema, com base nos critérios previstos na lei e nas boas práticas; a avaliação preliminar é obrigatória para sistemas de IA generativa e de propósito geral.
clauses.translated_text: [Unofficial translation of paraphrase] Before placing on the market, deployment or use, the AI agent may carry out a preliminary assessment to determine the system's risk level, based on the criteria in the law and good practice; the preliminary assessment is mandatory for generative and general-purpose AI systems.
clauses.requirement: optional self-classification for most systems; mandatory for generative/general-purpose AI
clauses.condition: before placing on the market or use
clauses.purpose: classify systems to determine applicable obligations
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI systems; mandatory for generative and general-purpose AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: Câmara avulso excerpt shows 'poderá realizar avaliação preliminar'; the mandatory requirement for generative/general-purpose AI is reported by secondary sources and may sit in a different article. Modality MAY for the general rule (MUST for GPAI/GenAI).

clauses.original_text: [Paráfrase — não é o texto oficial] Consideram-se de alto risco os sistemas de IA empregados em finalidades e contextos como: dispositivos de segurança na gestão de infraestruturas críticas; educação e formação profissional (acesso, admissão e avaliação); recrutamento, seleção, promoção e decisões sobre relações de trabalho; avaliação de critérios de acesso a serviços públicos e privados essenciais; priorização de serviços de emergência; administração da justiça; veículos autônomos; aplicações na área da saúde; e investigação criminal e segurança pública, entre outros, podendo a autoridade competente atualizar a lista.
clauses.translated_text: [Unofficial translation of paraphrase] AI systems used for purposes and in contexts such as the following are considered high-risk: safety components in critical infrastructure management; education and vocational training (access, admission and evaluation); recruitment, selection, promotion and employment-relationship decisions; evaluating eligibility for essential public and private services; prioritization of emergency services; administration of justice; autonomous vehicles; health applications; and criminal investigation and public security, among others, with the competent authority able to update the list.
clauses.actor: legislator / competent authority (classification); AI agents (subject to obligations)
clauses.object: AI systems in listed use contexts
clauses.requirement: systems in listed contexts are subject to high-risk governance obligations
clauses.condition: use in a listed purpose/context
clauses.purpose: focus obligations on uses that can significantly affect rights and safety
clauses.affected_asset: fundamental rights, health, safety, access to essential services, employment
clauses.applicable_systems: high-risk AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase of the high-risk list; items and wording not verified against the official text, and the Senate removed some items (e.g. certain content-curation/recommendation systems) during negotiation — check final list.

clauses.original_text: [Paráfrase — não é o texto oficial] A avaliação de impacto algorítmico de sistemas de IA é obrigação do desenvolvedor e/ou do aplicador sempre que o sistema for considerado de alto risco, devendo ser realizada antes da colocação no mercado ou uso e atualizada periodicamente ao longo do ciclo de vida; as conclusões da avaliação de impacto algorítmico serão públicas, observados os segredos comercial e industrial.
clauses.translated_text: [Unofficial translation of paraphrase] An algorithmic impact assessment of AI systems is an obligation of the developer and/or deployer whenever the system is considered high-risk, to be carried out before placing on the market or use and updated periodically throughout the lifecycle; the conclusions of the algorithmic impact assessment shall be public, subject to commercial and industrial secrets.
clauses.actor: developer and/or deployer of high-risk AI
clauses.action: conduct and publish algorithmic impact assessment
clauses.requirement: perform, update and publish conclusions of an algorithmic impact assessment for high-risk AI
clauses.condition: system classified as high-risk
clauses.exception: commercial and industrial secrets protected in publication
clauses.purpose: identify and mitigate impacts on fundamental rights
clauses.applicable_systems: high-risk AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Search excerpts of the avulso show the section heading 'Da Avaliação de Impacto Algorítmico' at Art. 25 and the sentence fragment 'As conclusões da avaliação de impacto algorítmico serão públicas'; allocation between developer and deployer and timing details are paraphrased and unverified.

clauses.section: Chapter on administrative sanctions (article number not verified)
clauses.original_text: [Paráfrase — não é o texto oficial] Os agentes de IA que cometerem infrações às normas da lei ficam sujeitos a sanções administrativas aplicadas pela autoridade competente, incluindo advertência, multa simples limitada a R$ 50.000.000,00 por infração ou, no caso de pessoa jurídica de direito privado, a até 2% do seu faturamento bruto, publicização da infração, proibição ou restrição de participar de sandbox regulatório e suspensão parcial ou total do desenvolvimento, fornecimento ou operação do sistema de IA.
clauses.translated_text: [Unofficial translation of paraphrase] AI agents that infringe the law are subject to administrative sanctions applied by the competent authority, including warning, a simple fine limited to R$ 50,000,000 per infringement or, for private legal entities, up to 2% of gross revenue, publication of the infringement, prohibition or restriction from participating in a regulatory sandbox, and partial or total suspension of the development, supply or operation of the AI system.
clauses.actor: competent authority (SIA / ANPD and sectoral regulators)
clauses.requirement: sanctions available for breaches, up to R$ 50 million or 2% of gross revenue
clauses.condition: infringement established in administrative proceedings
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI systems covered by the law
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; the fine ceiling is consistently reported, but the revenue base (group/conglomerate in Brazil, prior fiscal year) and the full list of sanctions were not verified against official text.

record_provenance.notes: parl.ca and justice.gc.ca could not be fetched from this session, so the bill text was not accessed: all clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false) of the first-reading text based on law-firm summaries and general knowledge; section numbers refer to AIDA as enacted by clause 39 of Bill C-27 and should be verified. Status: AIDA died on the Order Paper on prorogation, 6 January 2025 (Parliament later dissolved for the April 2025 election). Minister of AI and Digital Innovation Evan Solomon has said AIDA will not be revived as such, and that new AI legislation may follow; as of the latest sources found (Aug–Oct 2026) no successor AI bill had been tabled. A privacy bill (C-36) reportedly tabled June 2026 does not include an AI act (secondary sources; not verified on parl.ca). Second-reading and amendment dates are from general knowledge and secondary sources. Penalty figures: up to the greater of C$25M and 5% of gross global revenues for s.38/39 offences (per Blakes summary); administrative/regulatory offence maxima (C$10M / 3%) from general knowledge.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] A person who is responsible for an artificial intelligence system must, in accordance with the regulations, assess whether it is a high-impact system.
clauses.actor: person responsible for an AI system
clauses.object: whether the AI system is a high-impact system
clauses.requirement: self-assess high-impact status per regulations
clauses.condition: in the course of international or interprovincial trade and commerce; criteria set by regulation
clauses.exception: federal institutions and national security bodies
clauses.purpose: trigger risk-based obligations for high-impact systems
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase closely following the reported first-reading wording; never in force. Ministerial amendments (2023) would have replaced this with defined classes of high-impact systems.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] A person who is responsible for a high-impact system must, in accordance with the regulations, establish measures to identify, assess and mitigate the risks of harm or biased output that could result from the use of the system.
clauses.actor: person responsible for a high-impact system
clauses.action: establish measures to identify, assess and mitigate
clauses.object: risks of harm or biased output
clauses.requirement: implement risk identification, assessment and mitigation for high-impact AI
clauses.condition: system is high-impact (per regulations)
clauses.affected_asset: physical/psychological integrity, property and economic interests of individuals; equality
clauses.applicable_systems: high-impact systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; s. 9 required monitoring of compliance with and effectiveness of these measures, s. 10 record-keeping. 'Biased output' was defined by reference to prohibited grounds of discrimination under the Canadian Human Rights Act.

clauses.section: AIDA s. 11 (Publication of description — making available / managing operation)
clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] A person who makes available for use, or who manages the operation of, a high-impact system must, in the time and manner that may be prescribed by regulation, publish on a publicly available website a plain-language description of the system that explains how it is intended to be (or is) used, the types of content it generates and the decisions, recommendations or predictions it makes, the mitigation measures established, and any other prescribed information.
clauses.actor: person making available or managing a high-impact system
clauses.requirement: publicly disclose a plain-language description of the high-impact system
clauses.condition: system is high-impact
clauses.affected_asset: public's ability to understand AI use
clauses.applicable_systems: high-impact systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase combining s. 11(1) and 11(2); list of required elements recalled from first-reading text, not verified.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] A person who is responsible for a high-impact system must, in accordance with the regulations and as soon as feasible, notify the Minister if the use of the system results or is likely to result in material harm.
clauses.actor: person responsible for a high-impact system
clauses.object: material harm resulting or likely to result from use of the system
clauses.recipient: Minister (of Innovation, Science and Industry, as designated)
clauses.requirement: notify the Minister of actual or likely material harm as soon as feasible
clauses.condition: use results or is likely to result in material harm
clauses.affected_asset: individuals' safety, property and economic interests
clauses.applicable_systems: high-impact systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; wording matches law-firm reproductions of the provision. 'Material harm' left to regulations.

clauses.section: AIDA s. 39 (Offence — making AI system available causing serious harm or fraud)
clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase — not official text] Every person commits an offence if the person (a) without lawful excuse and knowing that or being reckless as to whether the use of an artificial intelligence system is likely to cause serious physical or psychological harm to an individual or substantial damage to an individual's property, makes the system available for use and its use causes such harm or damage; or (b) with intent to defraud the public and to cause substantial economic loss to an individual, makes an AI system available for use and its use causes that loss.
clauses.action: make an AI system available for use
clauses.object: AI system likely to cause serious harm, or used to defraud
clauses.requirement: do not knowingly/recklessly make available AI causing serious harm, or AI used to defraud the public
clauses.condition: knowledge or recklessness as to serious harm (a), or intent to defraud (b), and harm/loss actually caused
clauses.exception: lawful excuse (para. a)
clauses.purpose: criminal deterrence of seriously harmful AI deployment
clauses.affected_asset: physical and psychological integrity, property, economic interests of individuals
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase; per s. 40 (as summarized by Blakes), conviction on indictment could carry a fine up to the greater of C$25M and 5% of gross global revenues (organizations). Applied to all AI systems, not only high-impact ones.

versions.note: Month from compiler knowledge; not verified on leginfo.

versions.title: Chaptered
versions.summary: Approved with frontier AI framework, transparency report and incident reporting duties.

changes.detail: Frontier AI frameworks and transparency reports

covered_entities: large frontier developers (frontier developers with affiliates' annual gross revenues > USD 500 million in preceding calendar year)
covered_systems: frontier models (foundation models trained with >10^26 integer or floating-point operations)
covered_activities: deploying new or substantially modified frontier models
exceptions: information whose disclosure would reveal trade secrets, cybersecurity or public safety risks may be redacted from published documents (with justification)
conditions: Frontier AI framework and catastrophic-risk reporting duties apply only to large frontier developers

Catastrophic risk = foreseeable and material risk that a frontier model contributes to death or serious injury of more than 50 people or more than USD 1 billion in property damage from a single incident (e.g., CBRN weapon assistance, autonomous cyberattack or serious crime, evasion of developer control)
documents.objective: Increase transparency and accountability of frontier AI developers regarding catastrophic risks, establish critical safety incident reporting to the state, protect whistleblowers, and create a consortium to design a public computing cluster (CalCompute).
documents.conflict_rule: Per secondary summaries, compliance with designated equivalent federal standards may be deemed compliance with incident-reporting duties (Cal OES may designate); local ordinances on frontier developers' catastrophic-risk management are preempted. Not verified against chaptered text.

record_provenance.notes: Chapter 138 / 2025-09-29 approval / 2026-01-01 operative confirmed via secondary sources and Governor's press release (search snippets). No 2026 amendment found in searches, but leginfo history could not be checked. Section subsection letters in clauses (e.g. § 22757.12(a)/(c)/(e), § 22757.13) are from the compiler's recollection of the chaptered text and should be verified. Federal preemption pressure via the Dec 2025 EO is noted as potential conflict, not a judicial finding.

clauses.original_text: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework applying to its frontier models that describes how it incorporates national and international standards and industry-consensus best practices, defines and assesses thresholds for catastrophic risk, applies mitigations, uses third-party assessments, secures unreleased model weights, identifies and responds to critical safety incidents, and governs these processes internally; the framework must be reviewed at least annually.
clauses.action: write, implement, comply with and publish
clauses.requirement: publish and follow a catastrophic-risk management framework, reviewed at least annually
clauses.condition: developer is a large frontier developer
clauses.purpose: manage catastrophic risks of frontier models
clauses.applicable_systems: frontier models (foundation models trained with >10^26 integer or floating-point operations)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text.

clauses.original_text: Before or concurrently with deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version, a frontier developer shall publish a transparency report including its website, a contact mechanism, the model's release date, supported languages and output modalities, intended uses and use restrictions; a large frontier developer must also summarize its catastrophic-risk assessments and results, and the extent of third-party evaluator involvement.
clauses.requirement: publish a transparency report at or before deployment
clauses.condition: deployment of new or substantially modified frontier model
clauses.exception: redactions for trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety or national security with stated justification
clauses.purpose: public transparency about frontier model capabilities and risks
clauses.applicable_systems: frontier models (foundation models trained with >10^26 integer or floating-point operations)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text.

clauses.original_text: A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering it; if the incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the developer shall disclose it within 24 hours to an appropriate authority (e.g., law enforcement or public safety agency).
clauses.recipient: California Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES); appropriate authority
clauses.requirement: report critical safety incidents within 15 days, or 24 hours if imminent risk of death or serious injury
clauses.condition: discovery of a critical safety incident

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 服务提供者提供的生成合成服务属于《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第十七条第一款情形的，应当按照要求对文本、音频、图片、视频、虚拟场景等生成合成内容添加显式标识（如在文本、图片、视频的适当位置添加提示文字或标志，在音频中添加语音或节奏提示）；提供下载、复制、导出等功能时，应当确保文件中含有满足要求的显式标识。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Where a provider's generation/synthesis service falls under Art. 17(1) of the Deep Synthesis Provisions, it shall add explicit labels to generated text, audio, images, video, virtual scenes and other content (e.g. prompt text or symbols at appropriate positions in text, images and video; voice or rhythm prompts in audio); when offering download, copy or export functions it shall ensure the exported file contains a compliant explicit label. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.object: AI-generated text, audio, images, video, virtual scenes
clauses.requirement: perceptible AI-content labels, preserved in downloaded/exported files
clauses.condition: service falls within Deep Synthesis Provisions Art. 17(1)
clauses.purpose: inform the public that content is AI-generated
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI and deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording could not be fetched. Technical label forms specified in GB 45438-2025.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 服务提供者应当按照《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第十六条的规定，在生成合成内容的文件元数据中添加隐式标识，隐式标识包含生成合成内容属性信息、服务提供者名称或者编码、内容编号等制作要素信息；鼓励服务提供者在生成合成内容中添加数字水印等形式的隐式标识。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Pursuant to Art. 16 of the Deep Synthesis Provisions, providers shall add implicit labels in the file metadata of generated/synthesised content, containing production-element information such as the content's generated/synthetic attribute, the provider's name or code, and a content ID; providers are encouraged to add implicit labels such as digital watermarks in the content. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.requirement: machine-readable provenance metadata (attribute, provider, content ID); watermarks encouraged
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI and deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Watermarking is encouraged (SHOULD) while metadata labels are mandatory.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 提供网络信息内容传播服务的服务提供者应当核验文件元数据中是否含有隐式标识：含有的，应当在发布内容周边添加显著提示标识；未核验到隐式标识但用户声明为生成合成内容的，提示公众该内容可能为生成合成内容；均未核验到但检测到显式标识或其他生成合成痕迹的，识别为疑似生成合成内容并添加提示；并在元数据中添加传播平台名称或编码、内容编号等传播要素信息。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Providers of online content dissemination services shall check whether file metadata contains implicit labels: if so, add a prominent notice around the published content; if no implicit label is found but the user declares the content AI-generated, notify the public that it may be AI-generated; if neither but explicit labels or other generation traces are detected, identify it as suspected AI-generated content and add a notice; and add dissemination information (platform name or code, content ID) to the metadata. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.action: verify implicit labels and add prominent notices (confirmed / possible / suspected)
clauses.object: content uploaded and disseminated on the platform
clauses.requirement: tiered detection-and-labeling of AI content at distribution
clauses.condition: applies when disseminating content
clauses.applicable_systems: social media, video and other content platforms
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Three-tier confirmed/possible/suspected labeling is the distinctive feature.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 用户申请服务提供者提供没有添加显式标识的生成合成内容的，服务提供者可以在通过用户协议明确用户的标识义务和使用责任后，提供不含显式标识的生成合成内容，并依法留存提供对象信息等相关日志不少于六个月。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Where a user requests generated content without explicit labels, the provider may supply it after the user agreement makes clear the user's labeling obligations and responsibilities, and shall retain related logs (e.g. recipient information) for no less than six months. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.action: provide unlabelled content on request; retain logs
clauses.requirement: unlabelled output permitted only with user-agreement terms and >= 6 months log retention
clauses.condition: user requests unlabelled content
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI and deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Implicit (metadata) labels are not waived by this provision as the compiler understands it.

clauses.original_text: [Paraphrase, not verbatim] 用户使用网络信息内容传播服务发布生成合成内容的，应当主动声明并使用服务提供者提供的标识功能进行标识。任何组织和个人不得恶意删除、篡改、伪造、隐匿本办法规定的生成合成内容标识，不得为他人实施上述行为提供工具或者服务，不得通过不正当标识手段侵害他人合法权益。
clauses.translated_text: [Paraphrase] Users publishing AI-generated content via dissemination services shall proactively declare it and use the platform's labeling function. No organisation or individual may maliciously delete, alter, forge or conceal AI-content labels, provide tools or services enabling others to do so, or infringe others' lawful rights through improper labeling. [compiler's own wording]
clauses.action: declare AI content; not remove/forge labels or supply removal tools
clauses.requirement: user self-declaration plus ban on label stripping, forgery and label-removal tools
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI-generated content
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase from compiler knowledge; official wording not fetched. Combines a MUST (declare) with MUST NOT (tampering); modality set to the prohibition. Extends Deep Synthesis Art. 18.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当定期审核、评估、验证算法机制机理、模型、数据和应用结果等，不得设置诱导用户沉迷、过度消费等违反法律法规或者违背伦理道德的算法模型。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall regularly review, assess and verify algorithm mechanisms, models, data and application results, and shall not set up algorithmic models that induce user addiction or excessive consumption or otherwise violate laws and regulations or ethics. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.action: periodically audit algorithms; not deploy addictive/exploitative models
clauses.object: algorithm mechanisms, models, data and outputs
clauses.requirement: regular algorithm review/assessment; ban on addiction- or overspending-inducing models
clauses.purpose: prevent manipulative design and harm to users
clauses.applicable_systems: recommendation, ranking, filtering, scheduling and generative algorithms used in information services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Combines a positive audit duty (MUST) with a prohibition (MUST NOT) on addictive models.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当加强信息安全管理，建立健全用于识别违法和不良信息的特征库，完善入库标准、规则和程序。发现未作显著标识的算法生成合成信息的，应当作出显著标识后，方可继续传输。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall strengthen information security management and establish and improve feature databases for identifying illegal and harmful information, improving inclusion standards, rules and procedures. Where algorithmically generated or synthesised information without prominent labeling is discovered, it may continue to be transmitted only after prominent labeling has been added. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.requirement: maintain illegal-content feature libraries; label unlabelled synthetic content before continuing to distribute
clauses.condition: upon discovering unlabelled synthetic content
clauses.purpose: transparency about synthetic content, content safety
clauses.applicable_systems: recommendation/distribution platforms
clauses.interpretation_notes: Earliest CAC rule requiring platforms to label AI-generated content; extended by CN_Deep_Synthesis_2022 and CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025 Art. 6.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当以显著方式告知用户其提供算法推荐服务的情况，并以适当方式公示算法推荐服务的基本原理、目的意图和主要运行机制等。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall inform users in a prominent manner of their provision of algorithmic recommendation services, and publicise in an appropriate manner the basic principles, purposes and main operating mechanisms of the algorithmic recommendation services. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: use of algorithmic recommendation; its basic principles, purpose and main mechanisms
clauses.requirement: algorithmic transparency notice
clauses.applicable_systems: algorithmic recommendation services
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'Appropriate manner' left undefined; violations sanctionable under Art. 31.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者应当向用户提供不针对其个人特征的选项，或者向用户提供便捷的关闭算法推荐服务的选项。用户选择关闭算法推荐服务的，算法推荐服务提供者应当立即停止提供相关服务。算法推荐服务提供者应当向用户提供选择或者删除用于算法推荐服务的针对其个人特征的用户标签的功能。算法推荐服务提供者应用算法对用户权益造成重大影响的，应当依法予以说明并承担相应责任。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers shall provide users with options not targeting their personal characteristics, or provide users with a convenient option to turn off algorithmic recommendation services. Where a user chooses to turn off the service, the provider shall immediately stop providing it. Providers shall provide users with functions to select or delete user tags targeting their personal characteristics used for algorithmic recommendation. Where a provider's use of algorithms has a major impact on users' rights and interests, it shall give an explanation in accordance with law and bear corresponding responsibility. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.action: provide opt-out / non-personalised option; tag management; explanation
clauses.requirement: non-personalised option or easy switch-off, immediate cessation on opt-out, user tag control, explanation where major impact
clauses.condition: explanation duty applies where algorithm has a major impact on user rights
clauses.applicable_systems: personalised recommendation algorithms
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paragraph breaks in the source were joined. Parallels PIPL Art. 24 on automated decision-making.

clauses.original_text: 算法推荐服务提供者向消费者销售商品或者提供服务的，应当保护消费者公平交易的权利，不得根据消费者的偏好、交易习惯等特征，利用算法在交易价格等交易条件上实施不合理的差别待遇等违法行为。
clauses.translated_text: Where algorithmic recommendation service providers sell goods or provide services to consumers, they shall protect consumers' right to fair trade and shall not use algorithms to apply unreasonable differential treatment in transaction prices or other transaction conditions based on consumers' preferences, transaction habits or other characteristics, or commit other illegal acts. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: prices and transaction conditions based on consumer characteristics
clauses.requirement: no algorithmic price discrimination ('big-data price-killing')
clauses.condition: when selling goods or services to consumers
clauses.applicable_systems: pricing and recommendation algorithms in e-commerce/services
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'Unreasonable' differential treatment is not defined; Art. 32 refers enforcement to other laws (e.g. E-Commerce Law, pricing law).

clauses.original_text: 具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的算法推荐服务提供者应当在提供服务之日起十个工作日内通过互联网信息服务算法备案系统填报服务提供者的名称、服务形式、应用领域、算法类型、算法自评估报告、拟公示内容等信息，履行备案手续。
clauses.translated_text: Algorithmic recommendation service providers with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity shall, within ten working days from the date of providing services, complete filing procedures through the Internet Information Service Algorithm Filing System by submitting information such as the provider's name, service form, field of application, algorithm type, algorithm self-assessment report and content intended for public disclosure. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: algorithmic recommendation service provider with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.object: algorithm filing information incl. self-assessment report
clauses.requirement: algorithm registry filing within 10 working days of launch
clauses.condition: provider has public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.applicable_systems: algorithmic recommendation services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity
clauses.interpretation_notes: The filing regime is reused by CN_Deep_Synthesis_2022 Art. 19 and CN_GenAI_Measures_2023 Art. 17. Changes within 10 working days; deregistration within 20 working days of termination (paras. 2-3).

record_provenance.notes: cac.gov.cn was not reachable, so clause text was taken from the LawRefBook/Laws GitHub mirror (preamble in that file: adopted 2022-11-03 at CAC 21st office meeting, with MIIT and MPS consent, effective 2023-01-10). The source_uri, publication date (2022-12-11) and order number are from compiler knowledge and were not fetched. English translations are the compiler's own (Claude); no official English version exists. No amendment found as of Nov 2026. The 2025 Cybersecurity Law amendment (effective 2026-01-01) adds an AI article (Art. 20) and raises penalties in a parent law but does not amend these Provisions.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者和使用者不得利用深度合成服务制作、复制、发布、传播虚假新闻信息。转载基于深度合成服务制作发布的新闻信息的，应当依法转载互联网新闻信息稿源单位发布的新闻信息。
clauses.translated_text: Deep synthesis service providers and users shall not use deep synthesis services to produce, copy, publish or disseminate false news information. Where news information produced and published based on deep synthesis services is reposted, news information published by internet news source units shall be reposted in accordance with law. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: deep synthesis service providers and users
clauses.requirement: no use of deep synthesis for fake news
clauses.applicable_systems: deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Para. 1 adds a general ban on using deep synthesis for legally prohibited information/activities.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者和技术支持者提供人脸、人声等生物识别信息编辑功能的，应当提示深度合成服务使用者依法告知被编辑的个人，并取得其单独同意。
clauses.translated_text: Where deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters provide functions for editing biometric information such as faces and voices, they shall prompt deep synthesis service users to notify the individuals being edited in accordance with law and obtain their separate consent. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters
clauses.action: prompt users to notify and obtain separate consent
clauses.object: editing of face, voice and other biometric information
clauses.recipient: service users; individuals whose biometrics are edited
clauses.requirement: prompt users to inform the depicted person and get separate consent
clauses.condition: where biometric editing functions are offered
clauses.affected_asset: biometric data, portrait and voice rights
clauses.applicable_systems: face/voice editing deep synthesis tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: The provider's duty is to prompt; the consent obligation itself falls on users (aligned with PIPL separate-consent rules for sensitive personal information).

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者和技术支持者提供具有以下功能的模型、模板等工具的，应当依法自行或者委托专业机构开展安全评估：（一）生成或者编辑人脸、人声等生物识别信息的；（二）生成或者编辑可能涉及国家安全、国家形象、国家利益和社会公共利益的特殊物体、场景等非生物识别信息的。
clauses.translated_text: Where deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters provide models, templates or other tools with the following functions, they shall carry out security assessments themselves or by entrusting professional bodies in accordance with law: (1) generating or editing biometric information such as faces and voices; (2) generating or editing non-biometric information such as special objects and scenes that may involve national security, the national image, national interests or the social public interest. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.actor: deep synthesis service providers and technical supporters
clauses.action: conduct security assessment (self or via professional body)
clauses.object: models/templates/tools generating or editing biometric or sensitive non-biometric content
clauses.requirement: security assessment for high-risk synthesis tools
clauses.condition: tool has the listed biometric or sensitive-object functions
clauses.purpose: pre-deployment risk assessment of high-risk synthesis capabilities
clauses.applicable_systems: face/voice generation and sensitive scene generation tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Para. 1 separately requires periodic review, assessment and verification of generative/synthetic algorithm mechanisms.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者对使用其服务生成或者编辑的信息内容，应当采取技术措施添加不影响用户使用的标识，并依照法律、行政法规和国家有关规定保存日志信息。
clauses.translated_text: Deep synthesis service providers shall take technical measures to add labels that do not affect user use to information content generated or edited using their services, and retain log information in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and relevant State provisions. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: all content generated or edited with the service
clauses.requirement: embed non-intrusive (implicit) identifiers in all synthetic content and retain logs
clauses.applicable_systems: deep synthesis services
clauses.interpretation_notes: Basis for the 'implicit label' (metadata/watermark) regime later specified in CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025 Art. 5 and GB 45438-2025.

clauses.original_text: 深度合成服务提供者提供以下深度合成服务，可能导致公众混淆或者误认的，应当在生成或者编辑的信息内容的合理位置、区域进行显著标识，向公众提示深度合成情况：（一）智能对话、智能写作等模拟自然人进行文本的生成或者编辑服务；（二）合成人声、仿声等语音生成或者显著改变个人身份特征的编辑服务；（三）人脸生成、人脸替换、人脸操控、姿态操控等人物图像、视频生成或者显著改变个人身份特征的编辑服务；…
clauses.translated_text: Where deep synthesis service providers provide the following deep synthesis services that may cause public confusion or misidentification, they shall place prominent labels in a reasonable position or area of the generated or edited content to alert the public to the deep synthesis: (1) text generation or editing services simulating natural persons, such as intelligent dialogue and intelligent writing; (2) speech generation such as synthetic voice and voice imitation, or editing services that significantly alter personal identity characteristics; (3) generation of images/videos of persons such as face generation, face swapping, face manipulation and posture manipulation, or editing that significantly alters personal identity characteristics; … [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.object: generated/edited content of listed service types (chatbots, voice cloning, face swap, immersive scenes, etc.)
clauses.requirement: prominent visible disclosure of deep synthesis
clauses.condition: service may cause public confusion or misidentification
clauses.exception: for other deep synthesis services, provider need only offer a prominent-label function and prompt users that they may label (para. 2)
clauses.applicable_systems: chatbots, writing assistants, voice synthesis, face/body synthesis, immersive realistic scenes
clauses.interpretation_notes: Items (4) immersive realistic scenes and (5) other services significantly generating/altering content were truncated. 'Explicit label' rules elaborated in CN_AIGC_Labeling_2025.

clauses.original_text: 任何组织和个人不得采用技术手段删除、篡改、隐匿本规定第十六条和第十七条规定的深度合成标识。
clauses.translated_text: No organisation or individual may use technical means to delete, alter or conceal the deep synthesis labels provided for in Articles 16 and 17 of these Provisions. [translation: compiler's own]
clauses.requirement: do not remove or tamper with synthetic-content labels
clauses.applicable_systems: any deep-synthesis-labelled content
clauses.interpretation_notes: Applies to everyone, not just providers.

The source_uri and the order number (No. 15) are from compiler knowledge and were not fetched. English translations are the compiler's own (Claude), not official; no official English version exists. No amendment to the Measures was found as of Nov 2026. The 2025 Cybersecurity Law amendment (adopted 2025-10-28, effective 2026-01-01) adds Art. 20 on state support for AI research, ethics norms, risk monitoring/assessment and safety supervision, and raises penalties under the parent law used by Art. 21; it does not amend the Measures' text.
